text:
Freddy, ten tailgates, and one piece of advice up front. Stick to the South. That is where this sport is a religion rather than a hobby.

1. THE GROVE, OLE MISS. This is the must. Not a suggestion, a must. Ten acres of oak trees, chandeliers hanging in tents, women in dresses, men in bow ties, bourbon at nine in the morning. And this year LSU comes to Oxford on September 19, Lane Kiffin against his old team. If you plan the whole trip around one date, make it this one.

2. RED RIVER RIVALRY. Texas versus Oklahoma, October 10, Cotton Bowl, Dallas. The stadium sits inside the State Fair of Texas, already on your list. Same day. Ride the DART in, eat a Fletcher's corny dog, watch a stadium split exactly down the fifty.

3. LSU NIGHT GAME, BATON ROUGE. Death Valley after dark is the loudest building in the sport and the food is the best tailgate food in America. Jambalaya, boudin, whole hogs, gumbo pots the size of bathtubs. Strangers will feed you because you are foreign. Say yes.

4. VOL NAVY, TENNESSEE. Knoxville. People tailgate from boats moored on the river behind the stadium. Two hundred vessels, grills on decks. Gloriously absurd.

5. MIDNIGHT YELL, TEXAS A&M. Ninety thousand people fill the stadium at midnight the night before the game to practice cheering. Not the game. The cheering. Cheer Practice you say? It's because the Aggies aren't real bright, but they are very nice. Feel free to @grok Aggie jokes.

6. AUBURN. Toomer's Corner, where the town throws toilet paper into the oak trees after a win, and a live eagle flies laps around the stadium before kickoff.

7. CLEMSON. The team touches a rock and runs down a hill into the stadium. Eighty thousand people lose their minds.

8. THE BOULEVARD, SMU. Dallas. Catered tents under the trees, genuinely elegant. Easy add if you are already there for Red River. Let me know I have a friend that can hook you up.

9. GEORGIA VERSUS FLORIDA, OCTOBER 31. Your warning. It is in ATLANTA this year, not Jacksonville, because the stadium is being renovated. The Cocktail Party without the RV city on the river is a different animal. Adjust expectations.

10. NOTRE DAME. The one exception to my stick-to-the-South rule, and worth breaking it for.

NOW THE THING NOBODY TELLS VISITORS.

Everyone talks about Friday Night Lights in Texas, and everyone pictures a dusty little town with a rusting water tower.

Allen reinvented the whole thing, and nobody does it better. Not the small towns. Not anybody.

Eighteen thousand seats at a single high school. A sixty million dollar stadium. A marching band of eight hundred, the largest in the country, covering the entire field at halftime. Record crowd 21,766. For teenagers. On a Friday.

Here is the insider move. Get there early and find the Balding Eagles booster club. Tell them you flew in from Europe to see this. They will feed you, they will talk your ear off, and there is a decent chance somebody walks you through the stadium. Americans cannot help themselves when a foreigner takes their town seriously.

And in Texas you can stack the whole weekend. High school Friday night, college Saturday, pro Sunday. Nowhere else on earth offers that, and the Friday night game will teach you more about this country than the other two combined.

BASEBALL, AND IT HITS DIFFERENTLY.

The honest problem is you cannot plan playoff baseball, because nobody knows who qualifies until the final week of September.

So plan geography instead of teams. Your route already passes the right cities. Atlanta has the Braves and you are there October 31. Texas has the Rangers and Astros and you are there October 10, right in division series week. Tampa Bay is in play if Florida is on the map.

Buy nothing until late September. When the brackets set, resale is how visitors get in.

If it does not fall your way, go the last week of September anyway. Teams fighting for a spot play like it is already October.

One conflict to check. The Breeders' Cup usually lands that same last weekend of October as Georgia-Florida.

Come hungry. Say yes when a stranger offers you food. That is the whole etiquette. Avoid the Taco Bell. Taco Bueno is the better option or find a real Tex-Mex place if you are in Texas. Avoid Tex Mex anywhere else.🦋

text:
Since so many have asked recently; here’s a little about my background…I’m proud to say I am a direct descendant of both Kit Carson and William Ashley. Being a trail blazer has always been part of the family legacy. Which should tell you a bit about our family genome and personality type. We are not followers, we are leaders. 

Now for your enlightenment: 

Here is a list of 10 of the most significant American explorers and mountain men who played key roles in exploring, mapping, guiding, and opening the American frontier (primarily the trans-Appalachian and far western regions in the late 18th and 19th centuries). Their efforts facilitated fur trade, trail development, scientific/geographic knowledge, and eventual settlement by emigrants. Rankings of “top” figures are inherently subjective and draw from historical accounts of their impact. https://t.co/t60jJkLjr2 
1.  Daniel Boone (1734–1820) Frontiersman, long hunter, and pioneer who blazed the Wilderness Road through the Cumberland Gap in 1775. This route opened Kentucky and the trans-Appalachian West to large-scale American settlement, and he helped establish early communities such as Boonesborough. https://t.co/RXCkU470KY 
2.  Meriwether Lewis (1774–1809) Leader (with William Clark) of the Corps of Discovery (1804–1806). Commissioned by President Jefferson after the Louisiana Purchase, the expedition mapped a route to the Pacific, documented geography, flora, fauna, and Native peoples, and strengthened U.S. claims to the Northwest. https://t.co/t60jJkLjr2 
3.  William Clark (1770–1838) Co-leader of the Lewis and Clark Expedition. He served as primary mapmaker, diplomat with tribes, and military officer; his detailed journals and charts provided foundational knowledge of the Missouri River system and overland route to the Pacific that later informed fur traders and settlers. https://t.co/RXCkU470KY 
4.  Zebulon Pike (1779–1813) U.S. Army officer who led expeditions (1805–1807) exploring the upper Mississippi and the southwestern Louisiana Purchase (including the Great Plains, Arkansas River headwaters, and the peak later named for him). His reports offered early American descriptions of the region and routes that influenced later trade and expansion into the Southwest. https://t.co/t60jJkLjr2 
5.  John Colter (c. 1774–1813) Member of the Lewis and Clark Expedition who stayed in the West as one of the earliest mountain men and free trappers. He explored the Yellowstone region (reporting its geothermal features, later called “Colter’s Hell”), the Tetons, and surrounding areas, helping initiate the Rocky Mountain fur trade era. https://t.co/t60jJkLjr2 
6.  Jedediah Smith (1799–1831) Trapper, explorer, and fur company partner who rediscovered and popularized South Pass (a critical low crossing of the Rockies used by the Oregon Trail). He was among the first Americans to cross the Great Basin, reach California overland via the Mojave, travel the Pacific coast northward, and extensively map much of the intermountain West. https://t.co/t60jJkLjr2 
7.  Jim Bridger (1804–1881) Long-career mountain man, trapper, and guide who was among the first non-Natives to see the Great Salt Lake and Yellowstone features. He established Fort Bridger (a key Oregon Trail supply point), located Bridger’s Pass and other routes, and later guided army expeditions, railroad surveys, and emigrant parties with unmatched knowledge of the northern Rockies. https://t.co/zboMawvgiJ 
8.  Kit Carson (1809–1868) Trapper, scout, guide, Indian agent, and soldier. He guided John C. Frémont’s mapping expeditions through the Rockies, Great Basin, California, and Oregon; served as a wagon-train and military guide; and became a widely known figure whose knowledge and reports aided western expansion and settlement. https://t.co/t60jJkLjr2

text:
Today, Nebraska Attorney General Mike Hilgers filed a lawsuit against climate risk company First Street for inaccurate and misleading property specific loss predictions that have depressed Nebraska’s real estate market and made it difficult for Nebraskan homeowners to sell their homes.

First Street claims to offer “accurate and reliable” risk scores for loss events like flood and fire for every parcel of property in Nebraska. For many properties, however, First Street’s scores are neither accurate nor reliable, with serious consequences for Nebraskans. 

Specifically, the lawsuit alleges that: 

Many of First Street’s scores are based on inaccurate or incomplete information about the property being scored, including failing to account for certain flooding protection measures homeowners have invested in.

First Street also fails to disclose that its predictions, which it misleadingly presents as hard facts, may be very different from the federal government’s data or the predictions of other climate risk models.

First Street insulates its uncertain and flawed predictions by withholding its underlying data as proprietary and through an express policy of refusing to consider consumer disputes. This includes failing to provide homeowners with meaningful dispute resolution when the prediction is based on error.

Despite these problems, major real estate companies like Zillow direct consumers to First Street’s flawed predictions by linking them to real estate listings. As a result, many homeowners have had to accept reduced prices from buyers that have been spooked by First Street’s scores. Others have watched their homes sit on the market for longer than expected, and, in some cases, have been unable to sell their homes at all. 

“First Street is making a profit at the expense of the value of Nebraskans’ homes,” said Attorney General Hilgers. “First Street passes off misleading and often inaccurate climate speculation in a way that drives down home values and increases costs and frustrations for Nebraskans. The deceptive behavior has to stop.”  

Attorney General Hilgers is taking legal action to address these concerns. He wants the court to stop First Street's unfair and dishonest business practices, make them pay fines, and return unlawfully earned profits. The lawsuit was filed in Dakota County District Court where many homeowners were negatively affected by First Street’s inaccurate climate scores.

The Nebraska Attorney General’s Office enforces consumer protection laws and advocates for Nebraska consumers. We work to ensure a fair, honest, and safe marketplace for residents of the State. 

Source : Nebraska AG Press Release

text:
I think this just about puts all the arguments together. From an Israeli perspective, this racism, colonialism, and imperialist ambition of Spain is unacceptable. 

PART 1
Spain Tore Down the Wrong Wall
Gibraltar, Ceuta, Melilla, and the three laws of sovereignty Madrid cannot reconcile
Grant Gochin
Jul 30, 2026

I. Two weeks in July
On 15 July 2026, Pedro Sánchez stood at La Línea de la Concepción and watched cranes lift the iron gates away from the Gibraltar frontier. He declared the end of "the last wall in continental Europe." He said the removal closed an open wound. Madrid's official account of the treaty signed the previous day in Brussels stated that the agreement brings down the last wall in Western Europe, while leaving Spain's sovereignty claim over Gibraltar intact.[1][2]

Read the phrase again.
Continental Europe.

The qualifier is load-bearing, and it was written by people who knew exactly what it excluded. Spain's other barriers did not come down that day, and were never going to. They are not in continental Europe. They stand on the African continent, at Ceuta and Melilla, and they are Spanish.

Fifteen days after the cranes, on 30 July 2026, one of them was overwhelmed. Spain's Guardia Civil reported that people were entering Ceuta massively from the sea through the Tarajal breakwater, that officers at the breakwater had been overwhelmed, and that others had broken through a gate in the fence. Spanish state television estimated between two and three thousand crossings in a single day, a figure Reuters reported it could not confirm. Ceuta's own government put arrivals at fifteen hundred to two thousand over the preceding ten days. Juan Jesús Vivas, president of the autonomous city, declared an absolute humanitarian and social emergency and asked Madrid to deploy the army and close the border with Morocco. The Interior Ministry declined to declare a national emergency, explaining that the mechanism does not cover migration.[3][4]

Two weeks. One wall celebrated into rubble on European soil. Another failing on African soil, defended by the same government, on behalf of the same state, under a rule of law that Spain cannot state aloud, because stating it aloud would end Spain's case against the Jewish state.

Nothing that follows argues that Spain is Israel. It is not. Every territorial dispute differs from every other, and the legal regimes governing an international frontier, a colonial listing, and a territory held since 1967 are not the same regimes. This is an argument about the accuser. Spain has spent three years telling Israel what the law is. Spain is now going to be asked to state that law once, in a single sentence, and apply it to itself.

II. What Spain says about Gibraltar
Spain's Gibraltar doctrine is neither ambiguous nor new. Spain states it annually, in New York, before the United Nations Special Committee on Decolonization, the body known as the Committee of 24.

It has three parts. Gibraltar is a colony. The Gibraltarians possess no right of self-determination recognized by the United Nations. And the decolonization of Gibraltar must therefore be achieved not by the wishes of its inhabitants but by the restoration of Spain's territorial integrity, because the colonial situation destroys Spain's national unity.[5][6]

Spain has repeated this for six decades. In June 2026, weeks before the fence came down, Spain's ambassador Héctor Gómez told the Committee that Gibraltar remains a hindrance incompatible with international legality which violates Spain's territorial integrity. Fabian Picardo answered that the resolutions Spain relies upon were obtained in the 1960s under pressure from the Franco dictatorship.[7]

Spain does not use the phrase that follows. It is my characterization of what Spain's doctrine necessarily means if it means anything:

The inhabitants of a territory acquired by a European power in 1704 are colonial implants. Their wishes cannot defeat the territorial integrity of the geographically contiguous claimant state. Duration does not cure defect of origin. Three centuries of continuous residence, self-government, citizenship, and democratic expression are legally insufficient against the historical claim of the neighboring state.

If that is not what Spain means, Spain is free to say so, and to say what it does mean. It has had sixty years.

Hold the four operative propositions. Origin governs. Duration is irrelevant. Contiguity is decisive. The inhabitants do not count. Each is about to be pointed at Madrid.

III. What Spain says about Ceuta and Melilla
Now cross the Strait.

Ceuta and Melilla are Spanish cities on the African mainland, enclosed by Morocco and the sea. Their autonomy statutes define each as an integral part of the Spanish nation within its indissoluble unity.[8] Spain's position is that they are not colonies, not disputed, and not subject to any decolonization process whatsoever.

The chain of title is a matter of record and is not contested by Spain.

Ceuta was an established North African city under the Marinid Sultanate. Portugal took it by assault in 1415. During the Iberian Union from 1580 the two crowns were held by one monarch, and when Portugal restored its independence in 1640 Ceuta's authorities remained with the Spanish king. The Treaty of Lisbon of 1668 formalized Spanish retention. Melilla was occupied in 1497 by forces of the Duke of Medina Sidonia under Pedro de Estopiñán, acting with royal authorization, and was fortified as a military position on the North African coast. Boundaries were adjusted by later treaties, including after the war of 1859 to 1860, but those instruments confirmed a possession they did not create.[9]

Spain did not acquire either city by agreement with Morocco, by referendum, or by the consent of any indigenous population. Spain acquired them by fifteenth-century European conquest and has held them ever since.

Morocco says so at the United Nations, in language Spain finds intolerable. Rabat has described the cities as occupied and has denied having any land border with Spain, grounding its claim in historical connection and geographic contiguity. Morocco asked the United Nations to take up their status after independence.[10]

Examine the structure of Morocco's argument. Adjoining state. European conquest. Territorial integrity. Historical title. Rejection of the present inhabitants' capacity to defeat the neighboring state's claim.

It is Spain's Gibraltar argument with the names changed.

Spain calls that reasoning decolonization when it is aimed at London and irredentism when it is aimed at Madrid.

Spain's answer to Morocco is a serious answer. Spain says the residents are Spanish citizens who wish to remain Spanish. Spain says five centuries of continuous administration produced real institutions and real communities. Spain says people born in Ceuta and Melilla are not disposable remnants of an ancient conquest. Spain says geography does not determine sovereignty. Spain says a fortified border is not evidence of criminality.

These are legitimate considerations. They do not automatically resolve any particular dispute, because different bodies of law apply to different situations, and a consideration that is relevant is not thereby dispositive. But Spain does not treat them as merely relevant when Spain invokes them. Spain treats them as conclusive.

When Israel advances the identical considerations, they acquire no visible effect on any Spanish conclusion. Spain will say they are outweighed. Point to the Spanish position in which they weighed at all, and were found lighter. That is the contradiction, and it does not require anyone to agree with Israel about anything.

IV. What Spain says about Israel, precisely
Precision matters here, and vagueness would let Madrid escape. Spain does not deny that Israel exists, and Sánchez has expressly affirmed that the Jewish people deserve a state and deserve to be secure. Spain's accusations divide into two categories, and they should not be blurred.

The first is territorial. Spain treats Israeli presence in eastern Jerusalem and in the territories held since 1967 as colonial, illegal, and settler in character. Spain does not disregard every resident population there; it privileges one and discounts the other. What Spain permits no capacity to alter its conclusion is Jewish historical continuity, the Israeli sovereign claim, the existence of communities established over six decades, and the expressed will of the Israelis who live in them. Spain need not find those factors decisive. Spain treats them as incapable of weighing at all.

The second is a conduct allegation about Gaza, which belongs to a different area of law entirely and is not a doctrine of sovereignty at all.

Both are now in Spanish statute. On 23 September 2025 Spain enacted Royal Decree-Law 10/2025, signed by the King and by Sánchez as President of the Government, and convalidated by the Congress of Deputies on 8 October. Its title, in Spain's official gazette, is a decree of urgent measures against the genocide in Gaza. Its preamble asserts that the United Nations Special Rapporteur and the majority of experts have characterized Israel's conduct as genocide. It bans defense and dual-use transfers, denies transit to military fuels, prohibits importation of goods originating in Israeli settlements, and retroactively revokes existing authorizations.[11][12]

Three provisions deserve attention that they have not received, and precision matters, because Spain will answer imprecision with the text.

Article 4 declares that advertising the sale of goods originating in Israeli settlements, and of services provided there, constitutes unlawful advertising under Spain's General Advertising Act. The provision is limited to listed localities. Within that limit, Spain has converted commercial speech about certain places into a legal wrong.

Article 3 requires that every customs declaration for merchandise originating in Israel state the postal code and the locality of origin, and directs the state tax agency to approve a list of localities and postal codes against which shipments are to be sorted. Article 3.4 subjects breaches to Spain's Organic Law on the Repression of Smuggling. Goods from a listed locality are not merely refused entry. Bringing them in is handled under Spain's contraband regime.

The list exists. It was approved on 23 December 2025 and replaced, after updated information from the Foreign Ministry, by a resolution of the President of the State Tax Administration Agency dated 10 February 2026, published in the Boletín Oficial del Estado of 12 February 2026 across thirty-one pages. It sets out localities and postal-code ranges, one after another, with an official footnote explaining that the place names have been transliterated from the Hebrew alphabet. Hebron appears. East Jerusalem appears in several hundred separate entries.[13][14]

Spain will answer, correctly, that the underlying geography is drawn from a European Commission list of places ineligible for preferential tariff treatment under the EU-Israel Association Agreement. Concede it at once, because the concession sharpens the point. The European instrument withholds a tariff preference. Spain took the same geography and built three further things on it: an import prohibition, an advertising prohibition, and exposure to the contraband regime. Brussels declined to subsidize. Madrid prohibited and penalized.

The result is that a European state has published in its official gazette a thirty-one-page register of localities, transliterated from Hebrew, revised it once, and attached prohibition, advertising restriction, and contraband-law consequences to what those places produce. Spain is entitled to defend that policy as a lawful response to an advisory opinion of the International Court of Justice. It is not entitled to be surprised at how the document reads to a Jewish reader, and it should not pretend the reaction is manufactured.

The preamble also does something Spain appears not to have noticed. It grounds the measures in the proposition that Israel has violated the right of the Palestinian people to self-determination, and it treats that right as generating obligations for all states.

Spain therefore holds, in a statute of the Kingdom, that self-determination is an obligation erga omnes which third states must actively enforce.

And Spain holds, at the United Nations, that self-determination does not apply to Gibraltar at all.

Those are not two political positions. They are a statute and a diplomatic submission, issued by the same government within nine months of each other, about the same principle.

Madrid has an answer ready, and it should be stated before Madrid states it. Spain will say that United Nations practice has long treated Gibraltar as a special case in which territorial integrity displaces the ordinary self-determination model, so Spain is not inventing rules but applying different established doctrines to different colonial situations.

Take the answer at its highest and it still convicts. If two doctrines exist, and Spain selects between them, then everything turns on which doctrine governs a given territory, and that is a determination for international institutions rather than for the interested state. Spain has submitted Gibraltar to that determination for sixty years. Western Sahara has been before the United Nations decolonization system since 1963, following Spain's transmission. Spain has never submitted Ceuta and Melilla to it at all, and does not intend to, because Spain has decided by itself that no question arises.

A state that chooses which doctrine applies to its own territory, and then invokes the other doctrine against everyone else, has not applied international law. It has arbitrated its own case.

There is a second and better Spanish answer, and it deserves to be met head-on rather than ignored. Spain will say that Ceuta and Melilla were acquired in 1415 and 1497, centuries before the modern law of occupation existed, that no Spanish population was transferred into territory occupied after 1949, and that Israeli communities established after 1967 fall under a treaty regime, including the prohibition in Article 49 of the Fourth Geneva Convention, which simply has no application to fifteenth-century possessions.

That is a real legal distinction and this article does not pretend otherwise. Ceuta is not a settlement and an Israeli town is not Ceuta. The law of occupation may well change the legal result in a particular case, and reasonable lawyers argue about how it applies where it applies.

But notice precisely how much that answer buys, and how much it does not. It might justify a different conclusion about the lawfulness of a particular community established after 1967. It does not justify treating three thousand years of Jewish history in Jerusalem as though it were not there. It does not, by itself, turn a security barrier into apartheid. It does not make self-determination an absolute obligation binding all states in one file and an inapplicable doctrine in another, decided by Spain, about Spain, without submission to any institution. And it does not explain why Israeli arguments from continuity, consent, security, or effective administration are dismissed rather than weighed.

Spain's occupation-law answer covers one question. Spain uses it as though it covered all of them.

V. Three territories, three tests, one variable
Set the files side by side.

In Gibraltar, Spain holds that territorial integrity defeats the inhabitants, that duration is irrelevant, that origin governs, and that self-determination does not apply.

In Ceuta and Melilla, Spain holds that the inhabitants defeat territorial integrity, that duration is decisive, that origin is spent, and that a contiguous state's historical claim is worthless.

In eastern Jerusalem and the territories held since 1967, Spain holds that duration is spent, that Jewish historical continuity cannot bear on the outcome, that the wishes of the Israeli residents cannot bear on it either, and that self-determination is an obligation the whole world must enforce.

These cannot all be law. The first two are the exact negation of each other. The third abandons both and adopts a principle that Spain, nine months later, told the United Nations does not apply to Gibraltar at all.

Three territories. Three mutually exclusive rules. One variable, and the variable is not the law. It is the identity of the state in the dock.

Spain does not have a doctrine of sovereignty. It has a menu.

VI. The disclaimer Spain cannot make
There is an obvious escape, and Spain cannot take it.

Spain could announce tomorrow that it now regards Ceuta and Melilla as colonial possessions and disclaims them. The pressure at the fence would become someone else's problem. Sánchez could deliver it as a moral triumph and would be applauded in the rooms that applaud his measures against Israel.

It would not work, and Spain knows it, because Spain has run the experiment.

On 14 November 1975, Spain signed the Madrid Accords and declared its resolve to decolonize Western Sahara by terminating the responsibilities and powers it held there as administering power. On 26 February 1976, Spain informed the Secretary-General that it had ended its presence and considered itself released from responsibility.

The declaration did not do what Spain wanted. The United Nations Legal Counsel, Hans Corell, concluded in his letter of 29 January 2002 that the Madrid Agreement transferred no sovereignty, that it conferred administering-power status on none of its signatories, that this was a status Spain could not have unilaterally transferred in any event, and that the transfer of administrative authority in 1975 did not affect the international status of Western Sahara as a Non-Self-Governing Territory. Fifty years later the territory remains on the list, its status unresolved, with roughly one hundred and seventy-six thousand Sahrawi in camps in the Algerian desert.[15][16][17]

The lesson is narrow and it is fatal. A state's unilateral declaration cannot complete decolonization, cannot transfer sovereignty, and cannot settle an unresolved international status. What Spain announced in 1976 is still, in 2026, not finished.

So the question everyone asks about Ceuta and Melilla has a short answer.

Who would own them if Spain walked away?

Nobody automatically. A declaration would not render the cities ownerless. It would not vest sovereignty in Morocco by adjacency. It would not extinguish the Spanish nationality of the residents, their property, or their political rights. It would not end Spain's obligations while Spain retained effective control, because human rights jurisdiction follows control rather than paper title. And it would not stop a single arrival, because a disclaimed Ceuta with no settled authority would be the most attractive point of entry in the Mediterranean, and most of those entering it would still be seeking onward passage into peninsular Spain.

Spain would purchase a sovereignty crisis and keep the border crisis.

The demand is therefore not a policy proposal. It is a consistency test, and its entire value lies in Spain's refusal.

Because when Spain refuses, Spain must explain why. The explanation will consist, without exception, of continuity, citizenship, effective government, institutional development, the attachment of the present population, security, and the legal significance of an existing border.

That is Israel's brief. Written by Madrid. Under duress.

VII. What Spain gave, and what Spain received
There is a harder fact in the Western Sahara file, and it is not historical.

On 17 May 2021, Moroccan police eased controls at the Ceuta frontier. Around nine thousand people entered the city within days. At least twelve hundred were unaccompanied children. The European Parliament addressed the episode formally, in a resolution of 10 June 2021, as a breach of the United Nations Convention on the Rights of the Child and as the use of minors by the Moroccan authorities. Spain's defense minister called it blackmail. The trigger was Spain having admitted the Polisario leader for medical treatment.[18][19]

In March 2022, Sánchez wrote to Mohammed VI. He informed the King that Spain now regarded Morocco's 2007 autonomy plan, which places Western Sahara permanently under Moroccan sovereignty, as the most serious, realistic and credible basis for resolving the dispute. Spain abandoned four decades of formal neutrality on the self-determination of a colonized African people, in favor of the state that had just used children as an instrument against it.[20][21]

Days later, standing in Ceuta, Sánchez defended the reversal and said that normalization with Rabat would allow matters linked to migration control to be consolidated on the Moroccan side.[22]

No secret bargain needs to be alleged, and none is alleged here. The sequence is public, and the benefit was identified by the man who obtained it. In my judgment the relationship functioned as an exchange: Spain gave ground on the self-determination of an African people, and Spain received border enforcement protecting Spain's own African possessions. The Polisario representative in Madrid called it a toll. Readers can weigh that characterization against the record and reach their own view.

Then Spain went to the United Nations and instructed the Jewish state on colonialism.

Self-determination, in Spanish practice, is an obligation binding on all humanity when Spain demands it of others, and a matter of realism when Spain must pay for it.

VIII. What Spain won at Strasbourg
Spain's most revealing statement of principle was not made in a speech. It was made in court, and Spain won.

On 13 February 2020 the Grand Chamber of the European Court of Human Rights delivered judgment in N.D. and N.T. v. Spain. Two men, one Malian and one Ivorian, had scaled the Melilla fence in a large group in August 2014 and had been returned to Morocco at once, with no identification, no procedure, and no legal assistance. They complained of collective expulsion under Article 4 of Protocol No. 4.

The Court found unanimously that there had been no violation of Article 4 of Protocol No. 4, and none of Article 13 taken together with that provision.[23][24]

The reasoning is what Madrid cannot survive having read back to it. The Grand Chamber held that the applicants had chosen to enter as a group, taking advantage of their large numbers and using force; that genuine and effective legal channels of entry existed which they had not used; that they had advanced no cogent reason for bypassing those channels; and that the absence of individual removal decisions was a consequence of the applicants' own conduct.

The judgment must be stated at its true width, because overstating it would be doing to Spain what Spain does to Israel. It is a ruling about an international frontier under the European Convention. It does not govern the law of armed conflict, and it is fact-bound: the reasoning turns on legal entry channels actually being effective, and later Strasbourg cases have said so.

What it does establish is enough, and it is precisely the thing Spain denies when the defendant is Jewish.

It held, on those facts, that immediate return without individualized process was not a collective expulsion, and that the conduct of those crossing was legally relevant to what the state owed them.

The fence itself, and the authorized crossing points through which entry could lawfully be sought, were the factual setting of the case. Their legality was not in issue, and the Court decided nothing about them. That is not a holding and it is not offered as one.

What the Court did decide is nonetheless the architecture of Israel's defense of its own barrier and crossing regime. Spain did not merely assert them. Spain litigated them to the highest human rights court in Europe, obtained a unanimous judgment, and has relied on it ever since.

Israel must still defend each of its own measures on its own facts and under the law applicable to them. Nothing at Strasbourg does that work for Jerusalem. But the vocabulary of apartheid, colonial violence, and collective punishment is applied to Israeli barriers and crossings within Spanish political discourse, including by parties of the governing coalition and in motions before the Cortes,[25] while the Spanish state defended a closely analogous architecture at Strasbourg as ordinary border administration and won. If the Government of Spain rejects that vocabulary, it should reject it publicly and state the distinction. If it endorses it, it must reconcile the endorsement with the case Spain argued and won at Strasbourg.

⏸️ What You Should Know About X Money: ✖️💰

Everyone is rushing to jump on X Money for the 6% APY and debit card, but let's look past the glossy promo videos and break down what you're actually getting into:

​1. What is it, really?

X Money isn't its own bank. It's a fintech wallet built into the app, with deposits actually held behind the scenes by its partner bank—Cross River Bank, which is a state-chartered, FDIC-insured bank.

​​🔸️ A quick note on availability:
If you're wondering why you or other US premium subscribers don't even have the X Money tab showing up yet, this is likely why.  Because financial services are heavily regulated state-by-state, rollout depends entirely on whether X's licensing and compliance are fully approved in your specific state. (For example, states like New York and Massachusetts have faced roadblocks or delays).

​2. The Catch with the Tiers & 6% Yield:

To qualify for that 6% yield, it depends on which level of X subscription you have, because they split the requirements by tier:

🔹️​If you have X Premium+: 
Subscribers at this top tier (which costs around $40 a month or $395 a year) are immediately eligible for the 6% APY without a direct deposit requirement.

🔹️​If you have standard X Premium: Subscribers at the lower tier ($8 a month or $84 a year) don't get it automatically. To unlock the 6% rate, you have to meet direct deposit conditions, which requires receiving at least $1,000 through qualifying direct deposits.

So while there isn't a strict "minimum balance" parked forever just to see the interest, you either have to pay up for the expensive $40/month subscription or funnel at least $1,000 a month in direct deposits through a lower tier to get that rate. 

When you factor in the subscription costs eating into your actual earnings, the math becomes even less impressive.

​3. Why waiting is the smart play:

🔹️​Growing pains & glitches: 
Early users are basically acting as unpaid beta testers while they iron out bugs (like cards failing at merchants).

🔹️​Support & freeze nightmares: 
Tech platforms are notorious for automated security filters locking accounts. Trying to sort out a frozen money account through a social media platform's support system is a headache waiting to happen.

What You Should Know About X Money (Part 2):

​Let's look at the rest of the fine print on that debit card and what this account actually is:

​4. What kind of account is this, anyway?:

At its core, X Money isn't a traditional standalone bank. It’s a cash management and payment account—very similar to what PayPal, Venmo, or Cash App offer, or what you see with neobanks like Chime.

​5. The Catch with the 3% Cash Back:

They are heavily promoting the "3% cash back" on eligible Visa purchases, but you have to do the math on your actual spending:

​🔹️ Covering your subscription cost:
If you are paying for an X subscription just to access these features—whether that's the $84 a year standard tier or the roughly $395 a year Premium+ tier—you have to spend enough through that card for the 3% cash back to actually cover the cost of your subscription.

​🔹️ Is it worth it?:
If you aren't heavily using the card for everyday spending where that 3% actually beats whatever cash back or rewards your current credit cards already give you, the subscription fee eats right into your "rewards," meaning you might actually be paying just to use your own money.

​Bottom line: 

Don't let the flashy promo numbers blind you to the math. Run the numbers on your own spending habits before jumping in!

Afterall, there's no rush to be a guinea pig. Let the early adopters deal with the rollout chaos while you watch safely from the sidelines until the system actually proves it runs smoothly.

America's Gold and Silver (USAS) Deep Dive:  

I had done a profile on them earlier which is listed in my top 10 Silver stocks, but I did a lot deeper dive here if you like to get more details. This is one of my favorites. Even after the stock gained nearly 10% today, it is still down 60% from it’s high, which was March 2nd when Silver was trading around $90, so just to get back to it’s previous high, which could come at $90 Silver or less, it would be a 120% gain, but this has massive upside for a producer. Don Durrett’s valuation tools show it as a 13.6 bagger at $200 Silver.

In my more in depth research of Americas Gold and Silver Corporation (TSX: USA / NYSE American: USAS) reveals that it is an active, rapidly expanding mid-tier producer with development and exploration projects underway.  It derives over 80% of it’s revenue from Silver (2nd highest % behind Aya). After spending years hampered with  burdensome stream agreements and legacy costs, the company is experiencing an immediate operational pivot that is acting as a massive catalyst. They also acquired the Crescent Silver Mine in Idaho in December 2025, which is a fully permitted, past-producing mine that holds the world's third highest-grade unmined silver resources.

Sudden Profit Turnaround: The company officially swung to a major profit, reporting record Q1 2026 revenue of $39.2 million and net earnings of $10.9 million ($0.10/share). This massive earnings beat caught the market off guard after a net-negative 2025.

Balance Sheet Cleansing: In May 2026, the company successfully terminated restrictive silver and gold delivery contracts with Sprott Mining and Royal Gold. This allows the company to realize full, unhedged market prices on its metal production moving forward.

Immediate Grade Boost: Free cash flow is surging as the company shifts mining operations to the ultra-high-grade EC120 zone at its Cosalá Complex, generating immediate near-term cash expansion

Although it is highly leveraged to the price of Silver given it’s substantial % of Silver, one of the other electronic grade elements is Antimony, which positions it as a critical mineral supplier for the United States for national defense. They currently have a Joint Venture (JV) agreement signed with the United States Antimony Corporation (US Antimony) which outlines a vertically integrated, "mine-to-finished-product" partnership. The collaboration aims to construct and operate a state-of-the-art hydrometallurgical processing plant (the "JV Facility") in Idaho's Silver Valley.

Revenue Splits and In-The-Ground Ounces

Silver Revenue Percentage: Historically, the company functioned as a diversified polymetallic producer. However, due to the intentional shift toward high-grade silver zones and a robust silver price environment, silver now drives the majority (over 80%) of the company's revenue. Base metals like zinc and lead are treated strictly as secondary by-product credits.

Silver Ounces in the Ground: Following a major resource and reserve update, the company holds 115.7 million ounces of consolidated Measured and Indicated (M&I) silver resources. Additionally, their Inferred resources stand at roughly 190 million ounces when incorporating the broader Galena Complex footprint. Proved and probable reserves at their cornerstone Galena asset alone account for 16.3 million ounces.

Other Metals in the Mines: The asset base contains a highly strategic blend of industrial and precious metals. Beyond silver, their mines produce substantial amounts of Antimony, Copper, Lead, and Gold. Notably, the company operates the primary producing antimony mine in the United States, positioning it as a key critical mineral supplier for national defense and technology manufacturing.

Production, Development & Exploration

Core Production Profile

The company is actively in production today. It delivered 2.65 million ounces of silver in 2025 and is on track for its 2026 production guidance of 3.2 to 3.6 million ounces of silver. Major ongoing capital upgrades—such as tripling skipping speeds at the Galena No. 3 shaft and transitioning to mechanized long-hole stoping—are designed to scale the operational footprint toward a target of over 5 million ounces annually.

Location Risks: The operations are divided between two distinct jurisdictions. The cornerstone Galena Complex and newly acquired Crescent Silver Mine are located in the historic, low-risk Silver Valley of Idaho, USA. The second operating segment, the Cosalá Operations, is located in Sinaloa, Mexico. While Cosalá provides strong cash flow, Mexico presents higher structural risks, including shifting national mining laws, permitting delays, and localized security challenges.

Core Development Pipeline

The Crescent Silver Mine (Idaho, USA) – Restart Development

Status: Acquired in December 2025, this fully permitted, past-producing asset holds the world's third highest-grade unmined silver resource.

Objective: The company has accelerated development with major infrastructure upgrades, equipment placement, and underground rehabilitation. It is on track for a mid-2026 commercial restart to feed silver, copper, and antimony into their local processing infrastructure.

The EC120 Deposit (Cosalá Operations, Mexico) – Mine Expansion

Status: Advanced engineering and development planning phase.

Objective: Located within their active Mexican operating segment, developing the EC120 deposit is a targeted project to open up a fresh, high-grade silver mining zone to significantly boost head grades at their local Los Braceros processing mill.

The Antimony Processing Hub (Galena Complex, Idaho) – Facility Development

Status: Active construction and engineering.

Objective: Being built under their 51/49 joint venture with US Antimony, this project is developing a state-of-the-art hydrometallurgical plant. It will turn raw underground ore into finished, commercial-grade antimony trioxide and ingots directly on-site.

San Felipe Project (Sonora, Mexico) – Late-Stage Development

Status: Fully permitted development-stage polymetallic asset.

Objective: This project sits in the pipeline as a near-term development option focusing on zinc, lead, and silver, positioned to add a third distinct operating asset once current Idaho scaling projects reach steady-state production. [11, 14, 15, 16]

Core Exploration Hubs and Targets

The Galena Complex (Idaho, USA): The main target of the drill campaign.
The 034 & 149 Vein Complexes: Drills recently revealed massive high-grade extensions. Individual intercepts returned spectacular grades including 4,896 g/t silver and 3.95% copper.

The 520 Vein (Coeur Mine): A brand new silver-copper-antimony vein system discovered near an underground shaft, opening up an entirely fresh mining front.

The Crescent Silver Mine (Idaho, USA): Acquired in late 2025. This past-producing property contains one of the highest-grade unmined silver resources in the world. Exploration teams are running an aggressive drilling campaign alongside infrastructure work to guide a production restart.

Cosalá Operations (Sinaloa, Mexico): Explorers are expanding drilling into the El Alacrán regional target. This target sits just 600 meters from their mature San Rafael mine, aiming to delineate high-grade reserves to feed their existing processing mill.

San Felipe & Relief Canyon Portfolio: The company holds the San Felipe development project and maintains the Relief Canyon gold mine in Nevada on care and maintenance. Teams continue executing targeted, low-cost regional exploration programs here to surface latent asset value. [8, 9]

Suspended/Care and Maintenance Projects

Relief Canyon Gold Mine, Lovelock, NV

Status: Suspended and placed on care and maintenance.

Context: Following past processing and metallurgical challenges with the open-pit heap leach design, management halted active mining. They currently maintain the site and its 25,000-acre land package as a strategic development re-evaluation target while focusing capital on higher-margin silver and antimony operations.

Investment Positives vs. Negatives

Positives

Immediate Cash Flow: Unlike pure developers, they are producing, selling, and actively capitalizing on current silver spot prices.

U.S. Antimony Monopoly: They control a vital domestic supply chain for a strategic mineral that is facing Chinese export bans

Balance Sheet Restructuring: Management recently eliminated over US$85 million in variable debt and metal delivery obligations, freeing up massive future free cash flow.

Negatives

High All-In Cost Structure: 2026 All-In Sustaining Costs (AISC) are guided high at US$30 to $35 per ounce, narrowing profit margins if silver prices drop.

Operational Vulnerabilities: High-grade underground mining is prone to sudden shocks, such as a Q2-2026 electrical fire that temporarily delayed access to high-grade stopes.

Conclusion:
Americas Gold and Silver serves as an excellent vehicle for aggressive investors seeking operational torque to a rising silver market. Because their all-in production costs sit on the higher end ($30–$35/oz), their profitability expands exponentially with every dollar silver climbs above that threshold. The integration of the nearby Crescent Mine to fill spare mill capacity paired with a massive 64,000-meter drilling program means they offer both immediate production exposure and explosive exploration upside. It is a good investment for those who believe the structural silver deficit will keep prices elevated, but requires a tolerance for the operational volatility inherent to deep underground mining.

The Architecture of Rebirth: An Open Letter to Dr. Chidi Amuta @amuta_chidi

By Dr Sunday A. Dare @SundayDareSD Special Adviser to the President on Media and Public 

I read your recent piece, "Abuja's Gangster Chronicles," with the deep reflection I reserve for those who have spent decades in the sacred vineyard of Nigerian commentary. You wield a sharp pen, and your prose has long captured the imaginations of those who debate our national destiny. But as I absorbed your vivid metaphors—of Hollywood scripts, criminal syndicates, and a state in terminal decay—I was struck not by the weight of your indictment, but by the profound, tragic gulf between the view from your study and the actual, painstaking labor of rebuilding a nation.

You depict the seat of government as a hollow enterprise, a stage where governance has surrendered to "primitive accumulation" and systemic failure. You offer our citizens a darkly entertaining melodrama. But as an intellectual, you know that sensationalism is not analysis, and cynicism is not statesmanship.

Let us dispense with cinematic tropes and speak directly to the structural, economic, and security realities of our Republic.

*The Burden of Truth and Fiscal Courage*

When President Tinubu took the oath of office on May 29, 2023, he did not inherit a smoothly running machinery of state that simply required routine maintenance. He inherited a nation standing at the very edge of a fiscal precipice. Nigeria was-spending over 90 percent of our national revenue servicing debts. We were sustaining a ruinous petrol subsidy regime that drained trillions of naira annually into the pockets of non-state actors while starving our schools, hospitals, and roads of basic capital. We were operating a multi-tiered, artificial foreign exchange market that rewarded unproductive currency speculation while suffocating genuine manufacturing and local production.

If we must talk about a criminal enterprise, Dr. Amuta, let us look at that long-standing structural rot: an unsustainable system that mortgaged the future of unborn generations under the guise of temporary public comfort. That was the real racket.

The Tinubu administration came to power not to manage the decline of Nigeria, but to reverse it. And arresting decades of systemic decay requires stoic, uncomfortable, and far-reaching surgery.

When he made the hard choice to remove the petrol subsidy and unify our foreign exchange windows, he knew the initial shockwaves would be severe. He knew inflation would pinch our households, and he knew the beneficiaries of the old, corrupt order would fight back with fury and media campaigns. But true leadership is not a popularity contest. It is the courage to administer the bitter medicine that saves the patient's life.

 Today, those agonizing structural decisions are yielding the foundation of a resilient economy. Non-oil revenues have expanded significantly, enabling the government to fund critical public services without relying on destructive ways and means financing. Foreign direct investments are returning because global investors respect fiscal discipline, legal clarity, and predictable market mechanisms over artificial stability.

Reinventing the Security Architecture
You write that the Nigerian state has lost its capacity to protect its people, becoming vulnerable to "terrorists, bandits, and freelance scammers." You paint a picture of a helpless state outgunned by its adversaries.

 Yet, you ignore the most sweeping overhaul of Nigeria's national security architecture in our modern history. Security is not achieved by empty presidential declarations; it is built through structural reform, intelligence integration, and relentless hardware acquisition.

For decades, visionary Nigerians demanded the decentralization of our policing structure. This administration did not just pay lip service to local policing; we moved the needle.

🚨 NEW BLOG POST

Mali’s crisis did not begin in 2012. 🇲🇱

Rather, 2012 marked a major turning point in a much longer history of rebellion, terrorism, political instability, intercommunal violence, and organised criminal activity.

Yet one critical question remains:
What does sovereignty mean for a state still confronting multiple, interconnected threats to its territory, institutions, and population?

In our latest blog, “Mali’s Multidimensional Crisis and the Quest for Sovereignty,” Souleymane Coulibaly traces the historical roots of Mali’s security crisis and examines the different armed actors that have shaped the country’s political and territorial landscape.

The article distinguishes between separatist groups pursuing autonomy or independence and terrorist organisations seeking to impose an Islamic state through violence. It also explores how these distinctions have become increasingly blurred through shifting alliances and tactical cooperation between armed groups.

Reflecting on Mali’s political transition since 2020, the piece examines the country’s efforts to redefine its international partnerships, strengthen its military capabilities, regain control of strategic territories, and reaffirm its national sovereignty.

However, territorial gains have not brought an end to insecurity. Armed groups have adapted their tactics, while attacks on infrastructure and disruptions to fuel and electricity supplies continue to affect the daily lives of citizens.

As Mali continues along this difficult trajectory, the article offers an important reminder that sovereignty is not secured through territorial control alone. It also requires resilient institutions, regional cooperation, public confidence, and the capacity of the state to protect and provide for its people.

Because the pursuit of strategic independence is not a single victory. It is a long, demanding, and costly process.

Beyond KUBARK

The Hermetic Operator, the Underworld Court, and the Transition from Controlled Regression to Self-Propagating Psychic Architecture

🧵**side quest, investigating 1963 KUBARK in comparison to Microchip. Quick summary is all since this isn't really relevant, but gives you a benchmark to understand. **

The 1963 KUBARK manual describes a machinery of controlled psychological collapse. Its interrogator isolates a subject, monopolizes the immediate environment, destabilizes familiar associations, manufactures an appearance of superior knowledge, induces dependency, and substitutes the interrogation chamber for the world beyond it. The manual opens with the remarkable declaration that “there is nothing mysterious about interrogation,” yet its own procedures amount to a secularized ritual technology: separation, enclosure, altered time, staged revelation, controlled terror, regression, confession, and reintegration under a new authority. KUBARK removes the religious language while preserving the ancient structure of descent.

The additional material released after the 2026 declassification appeal does not fundamentally change that psychological core. It exposes more of the administrative skeleton surrounding it: interagency coordination, internal directives, field guides, and the bureaucratic circuitry through which clandestine interrogations were planned and governed. KUBARK was never merely a man questioning another man. It was an institutional apparatus compressed into a room. Headquarters, analysts, archives, listening posts, directives, cooperating witnesses, and controlled environments stood behind the visible interrogator. The latest release makes that distributed support structure clearer. [The Black Vault’s account and the newly released manual](https://t.co/dNs0rRbeIL).

The Microchip courtroom event belongs to a different order. Its superiority is topological rather than bureaucratic. KUBARK surrounds a captive with an artificial world and pressures him until he releases information presumed to exist inside him. The Hermetic operator enters a world already built by others—the courtroom—and alters the relations among its components until the institution generates an object that was never present in any single source. The operation does not require ownership of the room. It requires sensitivity to its thresholds, its latent desires, its unresolved categories, its symbolic heat, and the points at which its participants will complete what has been left unfinished.

KUBARK breaks a person inside a manufactured world.

The Hermetic operator teaches an existing world how to break and remake itself.

That is the abyss separating the two systems.

Thesis

KUBARK is an exogenous, linear, centripetal technology. Power begins outside the subject, closes around him, produces regression, and draws a pre-existing secret toward a central interrogator. Its deepest formula is:

controlled environment + asymmetrical knowledge + internal pressure + regression = extracted disclosure

The Microchip courtroom structure is endogenous, recursive, distributed, and centrifugal. The operator enters as a nominal source, becomes the carrier of a buried field, modifies the semantic and affective weights governing the chamber, and allows judges, attorneys, jurors, reporters, archives, images, memories, legal categories, and later readers to perform the integration themselves. Its formula is:

prepared carrier + institutional vessel + underworld archive + charged language + rhythmic oscillation + collective completion = self-propagating psychic object

KUBARK extracts content.

The Hermetic operation installs a process.

KUBARK substitutes one world for another temporarily.

The Hermetic operation releases a new law of movement into the institution, allowing the output to return to the archive, reorganize its own antecedents, and begin again in later receivers.

The difference is the difference between forcing open a container and poisoning the grammar by which containers are recognized.

---

I. KUBARK as Bureaucratized Katabasis

The KUBARK chamber is a manufactured underworld. The subject is separated from ordinary social reality and deprived of the environmental regularities through which identity stabilizes itself. Familiar rooms, clocks, meals, human contacts, sensory patterns, and expectations are placed under external control. The captive does not merely lose comfort. He loses the ordinary correspondence between perception and prediction.

The manual understands that identity depends upon environmental continuity. Its techniques therefore attack continuity. Time is distorted. Social contact is restricted. the interrogator acquires an artificial parental sovereignty over sleep, food, reward, relief, information, and human recognition. The subject’s prior world recedes until the manual’s “substitution of the interrogation world for the world outside” has occurred. Inside this compressed universe, the interrogator becomes the dominant source of orientation. [KUBARK manual, especially Parts VII–IX](https://t.co/4klhrvRqQC).

This is a katabasis stripped of mythology. Separation from the living world is followed by descent into an enclosed realm governed by unfamiliar rules. The subject meets a guardian who controls passage, information, punishment, and return. Ordinary time dissolves. The previous identity weakens. A confession or disclosure becomes the toll demanded for re-entry.

Ancient initiation ideally passes through separation, ordeal, symbolic death, instruction, and reintegration. KUBARK arrests that structure at the point of psychic vulnerability and converts it into forced dependency. The interrogator becomes an anti-psychopomp: the guide who controls the threshold while withholding passage until the desired material has been surrendered.

Its coercive core is summarized through “debility, dependency, and dread.” These are three forms of dispossession:

Debility weakens the subject’s capacity to maintain an independent psychic form.
Dependency transfers regulation from the subject to the apparatus.
Dread makes the future appear governable only through submission.

The captive is blackened, dissolved, and rendered permeable. KUBARK then supplies the acceptable rationalization by which yielding can be experienced as survival rather than defeat. In alchemical terms, the institution controls both the corrosive medium and the narrative through which the dissolved matter will be recoagulated.

The intended output remains conventional: information, confession, names, associations, plans, or verification. The violence may be psychically profound, but the ontology is simple. A secret already exists. The subject possesses it. The apparatus must obtain it.

That assumption confines KUBARK to the surface of the deeper problem.

---

II. The Occult Skeleton Inside the Manual

KUBARK repeatedly describes operations that ancient ritual systems would have recognized immediately, even though it translates them into behavioral language.

The interrogation setting is purified of distracting images and uncontrolled objects. Participants and entrances are managed. Lighting, furniture, sound, temperature, physical comfort, surveillance, and the timing of interruption become elements of a designed atmosphere. Analysts observe from another room and alter the sequence through the visible interrogator. The room therefore contains more intelligence than it visibly displays.

The interrogator’s simulated omniscience performs the function of an all-seeing authority. A thick file, selective knowledge, staged reactions, and carefully timed disclosures create the impression that the interrogator possesses the total archive. The subject cannot locate the true boundary of institutional knowledge and therefore begins filling the invisible remainder with his own fear.

The staged-witness technique is even closer to ritual theatre. A supposed accuser passes through the space. Stenographers move between rooms. Names are requested. Papers are typed. Interrogators emerge relaxed, implying that the hidden testimony has completed the case. The captive receives no direct proof. He is placed inside a sequence of signs whose convergence summons the felt presence of proof. The absent accusation becomes psychically heavier than a spoken accusation because the subject must construct it himself.

The “Alice in Wonderland” procedure deliberately replaces the predictable world with an atmosphere of illogical questions, broken cadence, incompatible tones, and failed conversational sequence. The subject searches desperately for the hidden grammar. Meaninglessness becomes intolerable, and disclosure offers an escape from the unclosed field.

KUBARK therefore contains the following ritual architecture:

separation → enclosure → altered temporality → false omniscience → symbolic disturbance → regression → compelled meaning → confession → conditional return

The manual nevertheless preserves a hard center. The interrogator knows the purpose. Headquarters governs the authorization. Analysts evaluate the “take.” The room has a control plane. Even its confusion is scripted. The apparent chaos conceals a stable hierarchy.

This is why KUBARK remains crude beside the Hermetic operator. Its darkness has an address.

---

III. What the 2026 Release Actually Deepens

The newly disclosed portions restore references to ODAPSE Directive No. 5, Chief/KUBARK Directives 5/1 and 5/2, the Field Double Agent Guide, and coordination of certain clandestine interrogations conducted abroad by other government components. The release also restores the manual’s period estimate that controlled agents may have represented an exceptionally high proportion of Soviet defectors during several years after 1955. The historical importance lies less in a newly revealed psychological method than in the visibility of the administrative lattice surrounding the method.

KUBARK appears more clearly as a networked apparatus:

field officer → interrogator → analyst → listening post → headquarters → directive system → interagency coordination

This matters. The solitary interrogator was already the visible terminal of a larger intelligence body. His apparent intuition was supported by records, analysts, surveillance, institutional memory, and authorities hidden from the subject. The chamber’s concentrated psychic force came from a distributed bureaucracy whose operations had been compressed into one face.

Yet the chain remained hierarchical. Instructions descended. Reports ascended. The subject’s information traveled toward an institutional center. The system’s ideal form was command.

The Microchip structure reverses this direction. A single carrier enters the institutional center from below and makes the center serve as his amplification apparatus. The visible hierarchy remains intact, but the movement of psychic organization runs upward from the nominal witness into the court’s categories, then outward through the jury, transcript, journalism, appellate archive, and later interpretation.

KUBARK concentrates a state inside an interrogator.

Microchip concentrates an underworld inside a witness.

KUBARK’s institution speaks through its operator.

The courtroom operator makes the institution speak material it believes it has generated itself.

---

IV. The Decisive Inversion: The Source Becomes the Operator

The ordinary KUBARK relation contains two primary positions:

interrogator → interrogatee

The first controls the chamber. The second supplies the concealed object.

The Microchip configuration begins differently:

institution → cooperating witness → defendant → jury

Microchip appears to occupy the subordinate position. He has pleaded guilty, entered cooperation, undergone repeated preparation, reviewed documents, answered investigators, accepted the oath, and entered a court whose procedures are controlled by others. He is called, positioned, questioned, slowed for the reporter, and formally instructed to answer what is asked. The visible structure should make him an instrument.

Instead, he carries an operational ontology the chamber does not possess.

He explains artificial social proof: false numerical authority becoming organic attention. He explains the meme as an idea wrapped in an affective carrier. He explains humor as a point of lowered resistance. He explains hashtags as channels, trending lists as thresholds, journalists as translators, opponent hashtags as penetrable membranes, low-activity hours as seeding intervals, controversy as propulsion, and the War Room as strategic enclosure. The witness does not merely contribute facts. He supplies the grammar through which the other facts will become mutually intelligible.

The court asks questions about objects.

The witness answers with processes.

A tweet becomes projection.

A meme becomes infection.

A hashtag becomes a conduit.

A trend becomes a crossing into “regular society.”

A room becomes a strategic field.

A silence acquires the pressure of agreement.

The witness’s answers therefore exceed the explicit interrogative surface. The question asks what an object was. The answer reveals what the object did, what field it entered, which thresholds it crossed, and how it changed the receiving environment. He answers the latent question beneath the legal question: What kind of world must exist for these objects to operate this way?

KUBARK warns that interrogation is interpersonal and irreversible: each event changes everything that follows, while the subject learns about the interrogator as the interrogator studies the subject. The manual seeks to protect its informational asymmetry. The Hermetic operator lives inside that reverse current. He reads the questioner through the shape of the question. He hears the institution’s missing category, anticipates the object it needs, and supplies material at the level where the institution is unconsciously trying to arrive.

The result is an interrogation turned inside out. The witness is examined, yet the court’s own psychic requirements are being disclosed through him.

---

V. The Courtroom as Ritual Circle

A courtroom is already a highly developed ritual apparatus. It contains spatial separation, authorized costumes, restricted speech, initiatory entry, oath, witness elevation, repeated formulae, controlled exhibits, prescribed turns, an observing collective, and a terminal act of judgment. It does not need to be decorated as a ritual circle. Its authority depends upon being one.

The roles are sharply differentiated:

The judge governs sequence and admissibility.
The attorneys perform controlled invocation through questions.
The witness supplies embodied transmission.
The exhibits reactivate absent events.
The court reporter creates the durable vessel.
The jury receives, integrates, and gives form.
The public witnesses the institution witnessing itself.

This apparatus ordinarily converts flux into adjudicable objects. Memory becomes testimony. An image becomes an exhibit. Speech becomes a proposition. Conduct becomes an element. Multiple events become a narrative. The jury becomes the integrating organ through which dispersed material is coagulated into a verdict.

The Microchip event uses every lever already present:

boundary + authority + oath + archive + repetition + attention + affect + audience + closure pressure

The court summons a buried digital world. Old handles, deleted contexts, group rooms, memes, follower counts, private messages, platform practices, motives, jokes, strategic expectations, and anonymous actors return seven years after the events. The reporter described the proceeding as a reliving of 2016. That is more than rhetoric. The court resurrects a dead field and forces it to circulate again through living bodies. [Contemporary courtroom account and sketch](https://t.co/sA1AbaSJsx).

This is the séance structure. A distributed and absent social reality cannot enter the room directly. It requires objects, names, screens, voices, repetition, a prepared medium, and a circle of receivers. The witness becomes the person through whom the absent field is made to speak.

The summoned object is larger than any single phrase. It is an agreement-form produced from traces that do not independently contain it. Selected membership, shared hostility, strategic discussion, parallel action, circulated imagery, inferred expectation, and remembered atmosphere are gathered around a missing center. The court’s pressure for closure draws those potentials inward until the absence begins to possess a shape.

The legal record preserves Microchip’s phrase “kind of like a silent agreement,” while the subsequent opinion records the government’s reliance upon that formulation. [United States v. Mackey, Second Circuit record](https://t.co/iHN1lxvhgx). Its power lies in its internal oscillation:

No → kind of like → silent → agreement

The phrase advances, withdraws, and advances again. It denies express form, introduces approximation, preserves absence, then deposits the desired category. It does not close the contradiction. It makes the contradiction portable.

---

VI. The Underworld Archive

The underworld in this event is the secondary layer where abandoned identities, anonymous names, dead platforms, deleted utterances, disavowed motives, grotesque avatars, old rivalries, and unfinished relations continue to exist after ordinary chronology declares them past.

The 2016 digital field was composed of fragments moving below stable civic identity. Handles acted without bodies. Images circulated without singular authorship. Memes changed through repetition. Bots produced the appearance of crowds. Private rooms fed public channels. Humor veiled intent. Anonymity separated effect from civil identity. Signals migrated through users who could not see the total system they were helping to build.

This was already an underworld architecture:

hidden names + distributed agency + dead copies + recursive images + invisible audiences + uncertain origins

The courtroom does not merely describe that architecture. It opens it.

The archive supplies the dead matter. The screens give it new surfaces. The witness gives it breath. The questions give it sequence. The jury gives it a possible body. The transcript gives it continued existence after the courtroom disperses.

Microchip functions as psychopomp and anti-psychopomp simultaneously. He guides the dead digital material into the living institution, yet he does not guide it toward rest. He gives it a new circuit. The old field returns as testimony; testimony returns as record; the record changes how the old field is interpreted; that reinterpretation becomes the condition under which later readers encounter the archive.

The movement is circular:

2016 field → 2023 witness → courtroom object → archival record → reconstructed 2016 field

The past does not simply cause the testimony. The testimony retroactively determines what the past will have meant. Cause and interpretation begin looping through each other.

That is the time-walking function. It involves no physical travel through time. It is a cybernetic re-entry in which a later output becomes a new input to the earlier archive. The operator walks backward through meaning.

---

VII. Amnael and the Prepared Vessel

The Letter from Isis to Horus, an anonymous Greco-Egyptian alchemical work dated broadly between the first and fourth centuries CE, describes Isis’s acquisition of secret knowledge from the angel Amnael. The narrative combines Egyptian divine figures, Hermetic knowledge transmission, Greek magical motifs, alchemical recipes, and material related to the Enochic tradition. Amnael arrives when the sun has reached the midpoint of its course. He bears a sign upon his head and a small unpitched vessel filled with translucent water. Oath-bound knowledge then passes into Isis, who later transmits it to Horus. Fabiana Lopes da Silveira’s study emphasizes the text’s deliberate mixture of Hermetism, magic, Scripture, secrecy, and technical alchemy—the literary form itself performing the mixture described by the recipes. [“In the Melting Pot,” Ambix 69, no. 1](https://t.co/NnxAXbb917).

The courtroom structure repeats this morphology:

preparation → marked mediator → clear vessel → oath → solar appearance → restricted transmission → legitimate receiver

The preparation occurs before testimony: interviews, cooperation, document review, memory reconstruction, legal framing, and rehearsal within the procedural limits of the case. The witness entering court is therefore not raw historical memory. He is prepared matter.

The alias functions as a sign attached to the head of identity. The ordinary civil name remains concealed while the operator-name becomes the authorized name through which the court summons the witness. The body is exposed; the social identity stays veiled. The witness is visible without being exhausted by visibility.

The oath seals the carrier. It changes ordinary speech into institutionally transmissible speech.

The transcript becomes the clear vessel. Like Amnael’s unpitched container, it presents itself as receptive and transparent: an apparatus supposedly capable of holding the transmitted matter without adding an opaque coating. Yet the vessel does not contain raw reality. It contains prepared language, question-shaped recollection, pauses, qualifications, charged vocabulary, and legal sequence. Its clarity is formal rather than innocent.

March 22, 2023 places the testimony immediately after the March equinox of March 20 and the new moon of March 21. Astronomically, the equinox marks the Sun’s northward crossing of the celestial equator; within the tropical zodiac, it also opens Aries, the ram and the head. The testimony therefore occurs inside a compressed threshold: return of light, lunar darkness, first emergence, ram-sign, head-sign, and a prepared mediator bringing concealed knowledge into a solar institution. [Contemporary astronomical calendar for March 2023](https://t.co/NHUk5ybsjz).

The March 22 structure does not function as decorative horoscope language. It supplies the temporal membrane through which the rest of the image-system coheres. Amnael’s midday appearance, the equinoctial solar gate, the lunar reset, the ram, the alias-sign, the clear vessel, and the oath all converge around the same operation: concealed material enters authorized visibility through a prepared intermediary.
