Dear @EricCortellessa,

In your report, you offer superficial assessments and omit structural facts that are indispensable for understanding both Venezuela’s history and its current reality.

To begin with, you suggest there are signs of economic recovery, citing renewed construction activity, better-stocked shelves, and a recovering oil sector. None of this reflects the reality on the ground. Microeconomic and social indicators demonstrate that Venezuelans remain in a state of extreme vulnerability, which explains why forced migration continues to grow.

Regarding the oil industry, you fail to mention that production barely hovers around one million barrels per day—far below the three and a half million produced in 1998. You also omit that the destruction of PDVSA was carried out, to a large extent, under Delcy Rodríguez’s leadership during her years overseeing the sector. Likewise, you ignore what the *Wall Street Journal* recently reported: major U.S. energy companies remain unwilling to make large-scale investments because they understand that the Chavista tyranny offers neither legal certainty nor the confidence required for long-term investment.

Describing Delcy Rodríguez as a "technocrat" is a serious analytical mistake. She is, just like her brother, a radical operative of the regime. Her administrative incompetence was laid bare after the double earthquake, an event during which the Venezuelan state effectively collapsed. According to reports from organizations such as Transparencia Venezuela, during the first 24 hours following the catastrophe, the state apparatus deployed barely 12.6% of its maximum response capacity, reaching only 34.6% after 48 hours and not attaining full deployment until eighteen days later, long after the critical rescue window had closed.

Behind that façade of supposed moderation lies a strategy of tactical survival. By cultivating a more institutional image, she seeks to buy time and give the de facto regime political breathing room, despite the profound rejection of a population that longs for the end of this criminal, kleptocratic, and failed system. Delcy Rodríguez was a key figure in the repressive apparatus, which included overseeing torture centers such as El Helicoide. Hopefully, international journalism will not allow itself to be deceived by this carefully crafted image.

Regarding her family background, the report states that her father was killed by security forces in 1976—a condemnable fact—but omits the broader historical and political context: he was a guerrilla leader involved in the kidnapping of foreign citizens, including William Niehous. The article also glosses over the fact that his crimes were investigated and prosecuted under a democratic system, unlike the crimes against humanity committed by Chavism over the past 27 years, which continue to enjoy absolute impunity.

As for the so-called "amnesty law," the claim that "9,000 people were released" is misleading. These were releases under arbitrary judicial restrictions and the precarious regularization of individuals who remain under the regime’s judicial control. Today, Venezuela still holds nearly 500 political prisoners, many of whom have been subjected to systematic torture, while their families have now spent more than 200 consecutive nights holding vigil outside the prisons. This human and legal reality was largely ignored.

Finally, regarding Venezuela’s democratic prospects, it is evident that neither Delcy nor Jorge Rodríguez intend to allow a genuine democratic transition. Their tactical objective is to weather the current political cycle and eventually restore the patterns of domination they have maintained for nearly three decades. They share the same ideological foundation and govern through the same model of power established by Hugo Chávez and Nicolás Maduro; only their corporate manners have changed. I hope that @marcorubio and the broader international leadership remain fully aware that the only viable path to regional stability is a genuine democratic transition, without concessions to authoritarianism.

I hope these critical elements will be incorporated and addressed with greater rigor in future coverage by this prestigious magazine and, perhaps, examined directly by you, @EricCortellessa.

text:
Clinical observation:
Over the last decade in my practice, I’ve sat with many people who use entheogens & plant spirit medicine(s). While many of their stories are beautiful and their experiences and visions are real, they are often still seeking the healing they went looking for. Of this group a smaller group tends to go chasing this to try to keep healing this way because it was very impactful for them or they felt better for a time. And of that group, an even smaller group becomes almost addicted to this kind of seeking and works with plant spirit medicine very often.

I’ve pondered over this a lot the last several years since it’s so common to see, especially the last few years and a few things are usually going on at once (and they tend to reinforce each other) :

+ The experience of a plant spirit medicine itself gets mistaken for ‘the healing’
People’s most profound journeys offer unbelievable, real insights into the soul of all things and our connection to that and how we are a part of that. People experience true catharsis or real contact with something larger and it deeply washes or wakes or resonates. However, this level of insight is not the same as integration into our being or body. Our 3D reality. We are here. We are in a life.
We have a day to day, a job, a need for food, this rhythm, and culture.

+ Integration has to happen in ordinary time. This is just in how someone speaks to their mother the next week, or whether they change a boundary around something, or whether they stay with a hard feeling without dissociating from tenderness or body or reality. This work is quite slow and unglamorous compared to the more wild, peak state of the entheogen, so it gets skipped or abandoned and then the person goes looking for their next experience instead of doing the afterwork of the last one, because its either too uncomfortable, heavy, hard or often it’s just boring. We might rather go out with friends that weekend than sit in and think out or feel on, ‘what have I just experienced inside of me?’

And so, related to that, we arrive at the nervous system: Our nervous system doesn’t hold a trait change from a state change alone. Someone can touch an *enormous* coherence during an entheogenic or mystical (swoon) experience and still snap back to their same very dysregulated baseline and chemistry once they’re out of it, because the underlying pattern (might be an attachment wound, or the person is in a chronic freeze state, or holding immensely unprocessed grief or anger) was never actually renegotiated with, just visited with in this very brief experience.

And so I just would say, if the terrain of our body doesn’t change, little can occur and it is the same for our spirits and what we choose to do. If our spiritual terrain does not change, the medicine (that many of the people I work with speak of) will keep showing them the same doorway and they will keep opening the doorway and turning around and around and around to keep going through it.

Lastly, there also can be a habituation curve. When there are repeated altered states without said integration, these experiences can start to function like other intensity seeking activities. This is where people may find that every round needs to go deeper or harder to produce the same emotional movement that the first one either did or hinted at, which looks very much like searching for the fix instead of doing it. 

Additionally, because I’m trained in some these bodies of plant spirit medicine, much of this ‘work’ is happening now without the ‘containers’ it was designed to come with : ongoing relationships w/ a teacher, or land or lineage, or community that holds someone accountable to what they saw. Your visions are not your endpoints. You carry what you see into your daily conduct, kinship and work. This is the work and container for YOU.
But if you take this framework away, people get very good at going out and not coming back.

text:
Magic mushroom compound could help defend skin against premature aging | Eric W. Dolan, PsyPost

Recent research published in the journal Biochemistry and Cell Biology suggests that psilocybin, the active compound found in certain mushrooms, might help protect skin cells from premature aging caused by poor diets. The findings indicate that psilocybin provides evidence of reducing inflammation and cellular stress in skin cells exposed to high levels of sugar and fats.

Skin aging is a complex biological process influenced by a mix of genetics and environmental factors. A diet rich in sugars and fats is known to accelerate this process by increasing oxidative stress throughout the body. Oxidative stress occurs when harmful, highly reactive oxygen molecules damage healthy cells and degrade structural proteins. This type of damage can weaken the skin over time, leading to visible signs of aging like wrinkles and a loss of elasticity.

When specialized skin cells called fibroblasts are exposed to excess glucose and lipids, they can become severely damaged. Fibroblasts are the primary cells responsible for generating the structural framework of human tissues, including the production of collagen. Over time, metabolic stress from a poor diet can push these cells into a state of cellular senescence. This means the cells stop dividing and growing, but they do not die off completely, which heavily contributes to tissue aging.

This state of cellular suspension causes the skin to lose its youthful bounce and structural integrity. The metabolic stress also triggers a state of chronic, low-grade inflammation, which further degrades the skin’s supportive proteins. Finding ways to protect fibroblasts from these specific dietary stressors could offer new paths to delay the physical signs of aging.

Psilocybin is a naturally occurring compound that interacts with serotonin receptors in the human body. It is primarily known for its psychological effects on the brain. However, these specific serotonin receptors are also present in other bodily tissues, including human skin fibroblasts. Past research indicates that psilocybin possesses potent anti-inflammatory properties, prompting scientific interest in its potential outside of mental health applications.

A research team led by Farzaneh Norouzkhani at the University of Lethbridge in Canada designed an experiment to explore how psilocybin might influence skin cells under intense dietary stress. They wanted to evaluate if the compound’s antioxidant and anti-inflammatory characteristics could defend fibroblasts against the damage typically caused by high glucose and high fat levels.

To test their ideas, the scientists utilized a widely used line of human skin cells known as BJ-5ta fibroblasts. They grew these cells in a laboratory setting, strictly standardizing the environment to observe the specific effects of different chemical treatments. The researchers established an aging model by exposing the fibroblasts to a solution containing 25 millimoles per liter of glucose and 400 micromoles per liter of palmitic acid for 48 hours. Palmitic acid is a common fatty acid found in many foods, and in high concentrations, it is known to cause cellular damage.

This high-sugar and high-fat environment was specifically designed to mimic the cellular stress of a severe metabolic condition. These metabolic conditions are known to speed up aging in human tissues by damaging cellular components. The scientists then tested the effects of psilocybin under two different experimental timelines to assess both prevention and repair.

In the co-treatment condition, they applied 10 micromoles per liter of psilocybin at the exact same time as the high-sugar and high-fat solution to see if it could prevent damage. In the post-treatment condition, the researchers waited until the cells had been stressed for 48 hours before applying 15 micromoles per liter of psilocybin. This second setup was designed to see if the compound could repair existing cellular damage. Every experiment was repeated three times in the laboratory to ensure accuracy and reliability.

The research team measured several different indicators of cellular health, starting with overall cell viability and rates of cell survival. They found that exposing the fibroblasts to the high-sugar and high-fat environment predictably reduced cell survival and increased signs of premature aging. Both the co-treatment and post-treatment with psilocybin helped preserve the overall viability of the fibroblasts.

The psilocybin treatments also tended to reduce the activity of beta-galactosidase, a specific enzyme that serves as a common biological marker for cellular senescence. Beta-galactosidase is an enzyme that accumulates in aging cells. By measuring its activity, scientists can estimate how many cells in a sample have entered a senescent, non-dividing state. By reducing this specific enzyme’s activity, the results suggest that psilocybin helped prevent the skin cells from entering a permanently arrested, aging state.

The authors also looked at a biological mechanism called apoptosis. Apoptosis is a programmed process of cell death that occurs when cells are damaged beyond repair or simply no longer needed. The high-sugar and high-fat conditions significantly increased apoptosis among the stressed fibroblasts.

The co-treatment with 10 micromoles per liter of psilocybin slightly but measurably decreased this accelerated rate of cell death. Applying psilocybin alone to healthy cells caused a small increase in cell death, hinting that dosage levels require exact tuning to avoid unwanted toxicity. This observation suggests that while the compound has protective qualities under stress, it must be applied in highly specific amounts.

The scientists also evaluated how the various treatments affected the cell cycle. The cell cycle is the orderly series of phases a cell goes through to grow, duplicate its internal components, and divide. The metabolic stress disrupted this natural cycle, abnormally trapping many cells in a specific phase where DNA synthesis occurs, known as the S-phase. Being trapped in this phase suggests the cells were struggling to complete basic life functions and were heading toward premature senescence.

Co-treatment with psilocybin appeared to restore a much more normal cell cycle distribution. This effect allowed the fibroblasts to resume standard growth patterns. By balancing the cell cycle, the compound provides evidence of helping skin cells maintain their normal, healthy functions despite a stressful environment.

The researchers also measured the expression of genes responsible for creating structural proteins. The high-sugar and high-fat treatment severely suppressed the genes responsible for producing collagen and elastin. These two proteins are entirely necessary for maintaining skin flexibility and structural strength. When psilocybin was applied at the exact same time as the dietary stressors, it significantly increased the expression of the elastin gene.

The research team also measured the activity of genes associated with driving inflammation in the body. They discovered that the metabolic stress massively increased the expression of several inflammatory genes in the fibroblasts. Applying 15 micromoles per liter of psilocybin after the stress had occurred successfully reduced the expression of genes known as IL-1 beta, IL-6, and COX-2.

These specific genes direct the production of inflammatory signaling proteins in the body. Reducing their activity suggests a notable calming effect on the tissue environment. This anti-inflammatory action likely helps protect surrounding skin cells from collateral metabolic damage.

Finally, the team conducted a specialized wound healing assay in their cell cultures. This test involved purposefully scratching a connected layer of cells in a culture dish and measuring how quickly the surrounding cells migrated to fill the empty gap. The metabolically stressed cells were noticeably slower to heal the artificial wound. The psilocybin treatments showed a tendency to encourage faster cell migration, but the improvements in wound healing were not statistically significant compared to the control group.

Because this research was conducted on isolated cells in a laboratory dish, the findings cannot be directly applied to living humans. This type of testing, known as in vitro research, is an early step in understanding complex biological mechanisms. It lacks the complicated, interacting variables of a whole, living biological system. The exact way psilocybin might be absorbed and processed by actual human skin remains entirely unknown.

Another notable limitation involves the exact mechanisms behind the observed cellular changes. The scientists suspect that psilocybin directly interacts with specific serotonin receptors on the fibroblasts, but they did not test this theory directly. Future research will need to intentionally block these specific receptors to see if the protective effects disappear. Taking that step would help confirm exactly how the compound works at a microscopic cellular level.

The research team also noted the need to compare psilocybin with established antioxidants and well-known anti-aging treatments. Testing the compound alongside common skincare ingredients, such as vitamin C or retinoids, would help identify its comparative effectiveness in a clinical setting. Future studies might also look at actual protein levels produced by the cells instead of just looking at genetic markers. This approach would provide a much more complete picture of the physical inflammatory response.

Exploring different types of metabolic stress and longer chemical exposure times could further reveal how psilocybin acts over extended periods. Clinical applications in the field of dermatology are still a long way off. This potential treatment will require extensive safety and dosing studies in animal models and formal human trials. Uncovering these specific details will help determine if topical formulations of psilocybin could eventually become a practical option for preventing age-related skin damage.

text:
Pennsylvania Game Commission Announces Start of 2026-27 Hunting Seasons

The Pennsylvania Game Commission reminds hunters that opening day for Pennsylvania's 2026-27 hunting seasons is Tuesday, Sept. 1, 2026, marking the beginning of statewide seasons for both Canada goose and mourning doves. The agency has also upgraded its online mapping center to enhance user experience for hunters and outdoor enthusiasts.

"For hunters, we're entering the best time of the year," said Game Commission Executive Director Stephen Smith. "The early season is upon us, marking the beginning of the new license year, a time when hunters across the state are making plans and preparing for all our exciting seasons ahead. On behalf of the Pennsylvania Game Commission, we wish all hunters a safe and successful year ahead."

The upgraded mapping center offers a cleaner, more user-friendly interface; faster access to maps and information; live data from authoritative agency sources; improved search, navigation, and overall performance. This platform is available on the agency's website and will continue to grow as new features and datasets become available.

"Most of us have become very reliant on our smartphones, especially when it comes to maps, so we wanted to ensure our enhanced mapping tool had better mobile functionality," added Smith. "Beyond that, it's a more streamlined tool with better search capabilities, updated symbols for map layers, and more. Updates will continue to be added throughout the fall."

The Canada goose season runs Sept. 1-25 in both the Resident Population Zone and the Atlantic Population Zone. Hunters are reminded that in western Crawford County and northwestern Mercer County, the season runs from Sept. 1-12, with a daily limit of one and a possession limit of three. In the Atlantic Population Zone, the daily limit is eight, with a possession limit of 24.

The mourning dove season begins Sept. 1 and continues through Nov. 27, 2026. The daily bag limit is 15 doves, with a possession limit of 45. The Game Commission has prepared more than 80 managed dove fields on state game lands to enhance hunting opportunities.

As a reminder, Sunday hunting is prohibited for migratory game birds, including waterfowl, doves, and woodcock, throughout the 2026-27 license year.

Licensed junior and mentored youth hunters can hunt ducks, mergansers, coots, gallinules, Canada geese, and brant statewide during a special Youth Day on Saturday, Sept. 19, 2026. All waterfowl hunting licensing requirements apply.

Hunting dogs are common partners in both dove and goose fields and are a valuable investment for many hunters. The Game Commission reminds hunters that in Pennsylvania, licensing your dog is required and can be helpful if a dog gets lost or separated while hunting. Visit https://t.co/94GVKPgKjS to learn more.

The Game Commission is also alerting hunters that its current mobile app has been deactivated. The agency's new "HuntFishPA" mobile app will be managed in conjunction with the Pennsylvania Fish and Boat Commission to provide a digital one-stop shop for hunters and anglers. The new app is expected to launch in 2027.

The Game Commission manages and protects wildlife and their habitats while promoting hunting and trapping for current and future generations. Those seeking information – including license requirements, laws, regulations, and more – pertaining to the upcoming hunting seasons can reference the 2026-27 Hunting & Trapping Digest or visit https://t.co/i2roDhI5G2.

text:
When I was a child and a  teenager, I loved video games – they were fun, it was about getting together with my friends and playing multiplayer, but I also enjoyed experiencing the adventures by myself.

Throughout the years, whether I was in the army going on real-life “adventures” in the Middle East or in training areas on and around Fort Bragg with the 82nd Airborne Division, I still played video games for the adventure and for the ability to escape reality. 

I know some “holier than thou” types on here say people need to “get out and touch grass”, but I touched more grass (and dust, and dirt, and all other types of natural surfaces) during my time in the Army than their entire bloodline has ever done, throughout history, so they can holster that shit.

I’ve been playing video games for almost 40 years, and I am now much more physically restricted, thanks to injuries that I sustained, and that have resulted from my extremely demanding jobs in the military.

I can no longer climb mountains, run through the woods, crawl through mud and train in forests that way I could as a soldier – and many of these games are my ability to do so.

A lot of people on here look down upon the gaming medium, they criticize you if you’re too old, they criticize you because they say you need to get your life together.

If they listen to their own advice, they would stop telling other people how to run their lives, and they would focus solely on how to run theirs, and they, going by their own advice, would completely close out all their social media accounts and become a bhuddist monk or some shit.

My point being is this – you can be an adult and play video games, you can have your shit together and be playing video games, you can get out and touch grass every single day and still go back inside and enjoy video games and the escapism it offers, there’s nothing wrong with that and there’s nothing wrong with you.

If anyone criticizes you for enjoying video games, and the escape from reality that it offers, that situation isn’t a “you” problem – that’s their problem… And feel free to let ‘em know it.

text:
Why the Jews of Toledo Opened the Gates to the Muslim Invasion in 711

In the spring of 711 a Muslim army of approximately ten thousand men crossed the Strait of Gibraltar from North Africa under the command of General Tariq ibn Ziyad. They defeated the Visigoth King Roderick at the Battle of Guadalete and marched north toward Toledo, the sacred capital of the Visigoth kingdom. When they arrived, the gates were opened from the inside. Both Latin and Arabic chroniclers record the same event. The Jewish population of Toledo opened the gates of the city to the Muslim invaders.

Tariq left Toledo and moved on to take more cities. He left the city under the protection of a garrison of Jewish soldiers, the same men who had risen up and opened the gates. When his master Musa ibn Nusayr arrived with a larger Arab force and took Seville, he too entrusted the city to its Jewish inhabitants until he returned. Cordoba, Malaga, Granada, Seville, and Toledo were all placed, at least temporarily, under the control of their Jewish populations by the Muslim conquerors.

To understand why requires understanding what the Jewish population of the Iberian Peninsula had endured for a century before the invasion arrived.

What the Visigoths Had Done

The Visigoth kings who ruled Spain from Toledo were Catholic Christians who had made the lives of their Jewish subjects almost unbearable through a relentless campaign of forced conversion, enslavement, and legal persecution that escalated decade by decade until there was almost nothing left to take.

In 558 Bishop Ferreol of Uzes ordered all Jews in his diocese to convert to Catholicism or face expulsion. In 633 the Fourth Council of Toledo declared that all Jews must be baptized and described those who resisted as ministers of the Antichrist. In 654 King Recceswinth forbade Jews from observing the Sabbath, keeping dietary laws, following their marriage customs, or circumcising their children. In 693 the Sixteenth Council of Toledo upheld the prohibition on Jews conducting commerce with Christians or doing business with Christians overseas.

Then in 694 came the decree that left nothing ambiguous. Catholic bishops issued a ruling that the Jews were traitors whose wealth should be confiscated and who should face perpetual slavery. King Egica had stated in Toledo just before that he had learned from reliable sources that Jews in Spain were working with Jews in other countries to conspire against Christians. Whether that accusation was true or a pretext for the confiscation that followed is debated by historians. What is not debated is what the decree said. Perpetual slavery. For an entire community. Because of their faith.

This was the world in which Spanish Jews were living when the news arrived that a Muslim army had crossed from North Africa and was advancing toward the heart of the kingdom.

The Invasion and the Decision

The Muslim forces that invaded Spain were not randomly targeting a prosperous Christian civilization. The Umayyad Caliphate had been expanding its territory across North Africa throughout the late 7th century and the invasion of the Iberian Peninsula was part of that systematic westward expansion. Tariq ibn Ziyad was serving the Arab governor Musa ibn Nusayr and the operation was a calculated military campaign.

What made it possible was the internal collapse of the Visigoth kingdom. King Roderick faced opposition from noble factions who disputed his right to rule. The kingdom was politically divided at exactly the moment when military unity was most needed. Jewish communities who had been told they faced perpetual slavery had obvious reasons to prefer any alternative to the existing order.

Both Latin and Arabic sources confirm that Jewish collaboration with the invaders went beyond passively opening gates. Jews reportedly served as guides and intelligence sources for the Muslim army, providing information about Visigoth military dispositions and the layout of cities. Arab historians are documented as agreeing that Jews both inside and outside Spain helped arrange the Islamic conquest. Jews traveled freely between Spain and North Africa before the invasion and had access to information about both sides of the strait that Muslim military commanders found valuable.

The degree of Jewish involvement is described even by the historians who find the account credible as uncertain in its full extent. What is not uncertain is that the Jewish population of Toledo opened the gates of the Visigoth capital to an invading army. The Jewish educational website https://t.co/X9b5I4TNzd, one of the most widely read mainstream Jewish educational platforms in the world, states this plainly in its own history of the Jews of Spain: the Jewish population of Toledo opened the gates and welcomed the Muslim invaders.

What Happened After

The immediate aftermath for Jewish communities was dramatically better than what they had endured under Visigoth rule. The conquered cities of Cordoba, Malaga, Granada, Seville and Toledo were for a time placed under the control of their Jewish inhabitants that the Moorish invaders had armed. Jewish communities experienced a period of comparative freedom and flourishing under early Muslim rule that historians have called the Golden Age of Spanish Jewry. Jewish scholars, physicians, philosophers, and merchants operated in ways that had been impossible under the Christian Visigoths. The great Jewish philosopher Maimonides was born in Cordoba in 1138, in a Muslim-ruled Spain whose relative tolerance for Jewish intellectual life had made his tradition of scholarship possible.

That Golden Age did not last indefinitely. As more extreme Islamic rulers replaced the early Umayyad administrators, Jewish conditions deteriorated again. When Christian kingdoms began their Reconquista and gradually recaptured Iberia over the following centuries, Jewish fortunes fluctuated depending on which ruler held power and what political use they had for Jewish merchants, physicians, and administrators at any given moment. Alfonso VI, who recaptured Toledo in 1085, was notably tolerant and offered Jews legal equality with Christians hoping to draw their economic expertise away from the Muslim kingdoms.

The story ended in 1492 when Ferdinand and Isabella, the same monarchs who funded Columbus's voyage in the same year, issued the Alhambra Decree expelling all Jews from Spain. The descendants of the people who had opened the gates of Toledo to the Muslim invaders 781 years earlier were driven out of the country entirely starting Spains Golden age literally.

KUBARK, Microchip, and the Dark Architecture of the Prepared Witness

The most disturbing sentence in the 1963 KUBARK Counterintelligence Interrogation manual is not one of its descriptions of isolation, sensory deprivation, fear, hypnosis, drugs, or induced regression. It is the manual’s quieter claim that the interrogation situation can sometimes generate the necessary pressure by itself. The room, the accusation, the asymmetry of knowledge, the isolation from friendly support, the authority of the questioner, and the subject’s uncertainty about what is already known may produce their own sequence of subjective events. The source begins to act inside a world that has narrowed around him. His previous world remains physically real, yet it loses practical authority. The interrogation chamber becomes the local universe in which speech, silence, resistance, surrender, guilt, time, and escape acquire new values.

KUBARK’s darkest intelligence lies in that change of scale. The manual does not treat interrogation as the neutral collection of preexisting facts. It treats it as the deliberate construction of conditions under which one person’s relation to facts, self, authority, and future action can be altered. Information is the declared object, but the operational medium is a human being’s organization of reality. The interrogator controls the environment, studies the source, disrupts familiar associations, manipulates uncertainty, and supplies a face-saving route from resistance to cooperation. The manual’s short-range objective is explicit: enlist cooperation or, if resistance persists, replace the resistant attitude with a cooperative one. Its language is bureaucratic, but the transformation it describes is profound. A person who entered as the custodian of a secret is to leave as a conduit for the institution that sought it.

The testimony of the cooperating witness known publicly as Microchip in United States v. Mackey permits a different and more advanced architecture to be seen. It is not a replica of KUBARK. No responsible documentary analysis can turn resemblance into a claim that the witness or the prosecutors copied a CIA manual, received clandestine instruction, or implemented a classified program. The relation is structural. Both records concern systems that convert a human source into a carrier of institutionally usable information. Both reveal that preparation, incentives, archives, setting, sequence, uncertainty, role, and controlled disclosure participate in the resulting account. The difference is that the direction of force changes.

KUBARK places the source inside a chamber and acts upon him until useful material comes out. In the courtroom sequence, the witness enters after years of institutional contact and after repeated review of an immense digital archive. He arrives under oath, under an alias, with his sentencing unresolved, bound by a cooperation agreement, trained by experience to understand audiences, and already fluent in the manufacture of salience. He is not merely the material being worked. He is also an operator upon the room. The source has become a transmission system.

That inversion changes everything. The KUBARK interrogator narrows one captive’s world so that the captive becomes dependent upon the interrogator’s structure. The prepared courtroom witness expands a historical world around multiple receivers so that they become dependent upon his vocabulary for integrating it. The first operation is centripetal: pressure contracts toward the source. The second is centrifugal: the source emits a grammar that reorganizes documents, memories, intentions, relationships, and absences across an audience. KUBARK aims to extract a bounded intelligence product. The testimony produces an interpretive field whose most consequential object—an agreement—cannot be pointed to as an express statement and therefore must be assembled from surrounding relations.

The resulting comparison is not between torture and testimony, nor between a secret service and a court as though they were morally or legally interchangeable. It is between two architectures of mediated truth. KUBARK exposes the primitive mechanics in unusually naked form: control the source’s environment; know more than the source knows that one knows; disturb the source’s familiar world; exploit the moment of disorientation; offer a path of relief; transform resistance into cooperation; preserve the output. The Microchip record shows those mechanics after institutional refinement and directional reversal. The source has already crossed into cooperation. The chamber no longer has to dismantle him in public. It can authorize him, protect part of his identity, regulate his rhythm, place an archive before him, and allow his account to act upon the receiving field.

The darkness lies in the apparent mildness of the later system. A coercive chamber announces that someone is being acted upon. Its walls, isolation, threats, deprivation, and asymmetry make domination visible. A prepared-witness system distributes authorship across lawful and ordinary acts: investigation, document review, meetings, plea negotiation, memory refreshment, witness preparation, protective measures, direct examination, cross-examination, redirect, judicial instruction, oath, transcript. Each component has a recognizable institutional purpose. Their convergence can nevertheless produce a phase change. The witness’s recollection becomes more organized, his identity becomes selectively visible, his language supplies causal coherence, and the audience performs the final integration for itself.

The older chamber breaks resistance. The later chamber can leave the receiver’s autonomy phenomenologically intact. No one needs to tell the listener what inference to make in a single naked command. The witness distributes cues, classifications, analogies, admissions, uncertainties, and compressed formulas. The listener experiences the completed narrative as an act of understanding. This is the critical advance from interrogation to psychic operation: the target supplies the finishing labor and therefore encounters the resulting object as partly his own.

The phrase “psychic operator” will be used in a precise analytic sense. It designates a person whose consequential action occurs through the organization of other people’s attention, expectation, affect, memory, inference, and narrative closure. “Psychic” refers to the psyche as the medium of integration; “operator” refers to an active function that changes the parameters under which meaning is assembled. It does not require telepathy, supernatural power, or an occult chain of institutional transmission. It requires something both more ordinary and more difficult to isolate: the ability to modify the conditions under which another mind converts fragments into a world.

Microchip’s own testimony supplies the vocabulary for this function. He described buying artificial engagement until human users inferred that an account must be worth following. He described humor as a vehicle that carried a message beyond the defenses ordinarily raised against direct assertion. He described inserting hostile material into an adversary’s hashtag so that it overflowed into an audience that had not chosen him. He described seeding low-activity periods before the morning news cycle. He described making ordinary material “weird and strange,” muddying a black-and-white universe, manufacturing the appearance of a “hidden army,” and trying to “infect everything.” He described a group whose coordination was real to him even when its agreement was not express. These are not metaphors supplied from outside the record. They are the witness’s descriptions of his own operating grammar. (Trial Tr. 485–510.)

The same grammar then returns at another level. The man who once manipulated visible metrics becomes a human metric of the invisible group. The anonymous account becomes an anonymous witness. The operator who used archives to generate controversies becomes a source whose memory is reorganized through “pages and pages and pages” of archived tweets and direct messages. The person who understood how a false appearance of magnitude can recruit organic belief enters a room in which his status as insider supplies social proof. The person who filled existing channels with foreign content enters the legal channel and gives its categories his own language. The person who described a hidden army becomes the visible carrier of a hidden collective. The person who understood propagation beyond origin gives testimony that will detach from his body and survive as transcript.

KUBARK called interrogation a continuum in which everything that occurs alters everything that follows. That principle is indispensable here. Microchip’s testimony cannot be understood as a transparent replay of 2016, extracted intact from storage in March 2023. It is the terminal public phase of a continuum: online activity; bans and identity reconstruction; voluntary contact and work with the FBI beginning in 2018; renewed contact after Mackey’s arrest; an April 2021 interview marked by uncertainty; tolling agreements; a guilty plea and cooperation agreement; postponed sentencing; repeated meetings with investigators and prosecutors; review of a vast archive; preparation for testimony; oath; direct examination; cross-examination; redirect; and preservation in the official record. Every stage changed the conditions of the next. The continuum did not have to falsify the witness to transform the form in which the past became speakable.

The purpose of this essay is to follow that transformation with maximum precision. It reads KUBARK not as a lurid catalogue of obsolete tricks but as a theory of controlled human mediation. It reads the Microchip transcript not only for propositions but for sequence, rhythm, incentives, archival operations, visibility, atmosphere, and the production of inferential closure. It asks what happens when the source is no longer merely interrogated inside a constructed world, but enters a public chamber carrying the capacity to construct one around others.

Thesis

The KUBARK manual and the Microchip testimony disclose two historically distinct but structurally comparable systems for converting uncertainty into institutionally actionable narrative. KUBARK seeks to control a resistant source by replacing the source’s familiar world with an interrogation world. It uses environmental command, asymmetrical knowledge, uncertainty, regression, dread, staged social evidence, temporal manipulation, and rationalized surrender to make cooperation easier than resistance. Its fundamental unit is a dyad: interrogator and interrogatee. Its desired product is information transferred from the source to the service.

The Microchip courtroom sequence reverses and distributes this architecture. The cooperating source has already entered an institutional continuum. His legal exposure, desire for cooperation credit, deferred sentencing, repeated preparation, protected identity, archive-assisted recollection, and ongoing relation with the FBI form the containing vessel before he takes the stand. Once sworn, however, he is not simply a passive repository from which counsel extracts data. He carries a developed operator-function: an ability to alter salience, manufacture apparent social magnitude, exploit repetition, convert humor into transport, enter existing channels, make ordinary material uncanny, and induce receivers to complete patterns whose decisive relation remains unstated.

The transition can be stated formally:

KUBARK: control the source → destabilize the source’s world → create dependence → supply a route to cooperation → extract and preserve information.

The prepared-operator courtroom: prepare and bind the source → authorize a partial identity → reactivate and organize an archive → distribute an interpretive grammar → induce receivers to integrate the missing relation → preserve the integration as legal record.

KUBARK’s subject is pressured to produce speech. The courtroom operator’s audience is invited to produce coherence. KUBARK attacks resistance directly or indirectly until autonomy contracts. The courtroom operation can work by preserving the receiver’s felt autonomy: the listener completes the narrative, experiences the completion as inference, and then returns to the evidence with a model that makes previously scattered fragments appear to have anticipated the completed object.

The principal novelty is therefore not a more extreme technique. It is a change in the location of the work. KUBARK places most of the transformational labor inside the source under interrogation. The courtroom operation transfers a substantial portion of that labor into the audience. The witness becomes less a container of facts than a differential process: wherever his vocabulary enters the record, it changes the direction in which surrounding facts are integrated.

The deepest comparison rests on five inversions.

First, the resistant source becomes the cooperating carrier. Second, the secret chamber becomes the public chamber. Third, pressure upon one captive becomes distributed pressure within an interpretive field. Fourth, extraction becomes injection: instead of drawing information from a closed psyche, the witness inserts a causal grammar into multiple psyches. Fifth, the finite intelligence report becomes a recursively active archive capable of reorganizing later readings of the past.

The dark achievement of the prepared witness is not that he overcomes the courtroom’s procedures. It is that he becomes effective through them. Oath gives gravity. Alias gives concentrated symbolic identity. questioning gives rhythm. Exhibits give external memory. Cross-examination exposes contradiction while also repeating the central objects. Redirect repairs the contradiction through an archive-mediated account of improved recollection. The transcript gives duration. Institutional regularity becomes the carrier wave.

I. Two Archives and One Structural Comparison

The argument rests primarily on two records. The first is the July 1963 CIA manual KUBARK Counterintelligence Interrogation, including the more complete official release approved in 2026. The second is the March 22, 2023 trial transcript containing Microchip’s direct examination, cross-examination, and redirect in United States v. Mackey, No. 21-CR-80 (E.D.N.Y.). The analysis also uses the cooperation terms and procedural facts read into that transcript.

The comparison is morphological rather than genealogical. No document establishes that Microchip studied KUBARK, that any participant intended to reproduce its techniques, or that ordinary federal witness preparation is a continuation of CIA interrogation doctrine. The absence of such evidence does not eliminate structural analysis. Institutions separated by purpose, legality, period, and formal design can still reveal homologous operations: source assessment, asymmetrical disclosure, archive control, role preparation, environmental framing, incentive management, narrative elicitation, credibility construction, and preservation of output.

Morphology matters because techniques change when they migrate across institutions. A mechanism rarely survives by preserving its original surface. Overt pressure may become contractual incentive. physical confinement may become control over which identity is disclosed. isolation may become a witness’s separation from prior social worlds. the interrogator’s dossier may become a jointly reviewed digital archive. the staged accusation may become an evidentiary sequence. the hidden listening room may become the distributed institutional team that prepares, observes, questions, and later cites the transcript. A practice can become more socially powerful as it becomes less visibly exceptional.

This approach also prevents two opposite errors. The first would sensationalize the record by calling every instance of preparation “brainwashing” or every ambiguity a covert technique. That would destroy precision. The second would atomize the record into ordinary procedural events and refuse to examine their cumulative organization. That would destroy the object of inquiry. The relevant question is not whether document review, cooperation agreements, pseudonymous testimony, direct examination, and redirect are each independently recognizable. They plainly are. The question is what kind of human transmitter emerges when those elements converge around a witness already skilled in manipulating collective attention.

The KUBARK manual itself demands such a continuum analysis. It insists that interrogation is an irreversible sequence in which each event modifies all later events. That premise can be detached from the manual’s coercive project and used as an analytic instrument. A witness’s account at time T cannot be separated from all of the interactions, incentives, reminders, archives, rehearsals, social relations, and expectations that precede T. The account may remain sincere. Sincerity does not stop cognition from being reconstructive, role-sensitive, and context-dependent. It means only that the speaker experiences the resulting account as truthful.

The primary transcript is unusually valuable because it exposes several stages of that continuum in open court. Earlier statements were read back. uncertainty was acknowledged. later archival review was described. the cooperation agreement was examined. the sentencing incentive was made visible. the witness’s ongoing FBI relationship was identified. the court regulated his pace and scope. the prosecution then repaired the apparent discontinuity by asking whether extensive review had refreshed his recollection. The witness answered that it had done exactly that and that his memory was now “very much” better. (Trial Tr. 537–550, 553–565, 594–597.)

That sequence is not proof of falsehood. It is proof that testimony has a production history.

II. KUBARK Was an Administrative System Before It Was a Technique Manual

The popular image of KUBARK is dominated by its most infamous pages: isolation, deprivation, fear, pain, hypnosis, narcosis, regression. The 2026 release makes another aspect harder to ignore. The manual belonged to a larger architecture of interagency coordination. Newly restored language identifies an internal directive governing KUBARK responsibility for coordinating certain clandestine overseas interrogations conducted by other departments and agencies. It refers to additional directives, station and base responsibilities, information requirements, and reciprocal coordination when another component’s interests were implicated. The manual was therefore not merely advice passed from one interrogator to another. It was part of a system for deciding jurisdiction, gathering preliminary information, distributing authority, avoiding uncoordinated action, and managing the institutional afterlife of what a source disclosed. (KUBARK 6–8; Greenewald 2026.)

That administrative context supplies the first important comparison. Human transformation is rarely the work of a solitary charismatic manipulator. The visible questioner is often the terminal point of a distributed apparatus. Files are assembled elsewhere. legal authority is negotiated elsewhere. detention or access is arranged elsewhere. liaison services contribute information. technical personnel record or monitor. supervisors approve. analysts determine intelligence requirements. future handlers decide whether the source can be used operationally. The interrogator appears as one person, but the system speaks through him.

The courtroom is organized differently and under public law, yet the cooperating witness is also a terminal point of distributed preparation. The March 22 transcript begins by establishing that Microchip had met the prosecutor many times, had met everyone at the government table multiple times, and had met the FBI agent. He had counsel. He had signed a cooperation agreement. He had pleaded guilty. He had agreed to possible testimony and assistance in other cases. (Trial Tr. 479–481.) Later cross-examination established approximately twenty contacts with government representatives, whether by telephone, video, or in person; continuing work with the FBI; recent meetings with prosecutors and agents; and a sentencing date postponed until after his testimony. (Trial Tr. 514–565.)

The institutional body behind the witness should not be confused with authorship of every word he spoke. That is precisely what makes the structure more complex. Agency is distributed rather than erased. The witness brings personal memory, motives, skills, language, and strategic intelligence. The government brings charging power, a cooperation framework, documentary access, repeated meetings, legal categories, a public forum, and control over whether to seek substantial-assistance credit. The court brings oath, admissibility, turn-taking, protection, and record. The lawyers bring narrative sequence. The archive brings externalized traces of a past too large for unaided recall. The jury brings final integration.

The resulting testimony has no single author in the naïve sense. It is produced at the intersection of these agencies. KUBARK’s administrative system makes visible a truth that survives beyond clandestine interrogation: before a source speaks in an institutionally consequential way, an organization defines what counts as useful, which history must be reviewed, what may remain hidden, what incentives attach to cooperation, who may ask questions, how answers will be recorded, and where the output will travel.

The newest KUBARK release also restores a period estimate that some Soviet defectors had proven to be controlled agents, with internal estimates at one point ranging as high as seventy percent. The figure was an intelligence estimate, not an independently validated historical rate, and it should be treated as evidence of institutional suspicion rather than statistical fact. Its significance lies in the source problem it encodes. The person who arrives offering information may already be carrying another system. A source can be sincere at one level, deceptive at another, strategically planted, partially controlled, self-interested, or reorganized by the institution that receives him. KUBARK therefore demanded scrutiny not only of content but of the source’s affiliations, incentives, previous handling, and operational future. (KUBARK 42–43.)

That controlled-source problem changes form in the courtroom. Microchip should not be called a controlled agent in the intelligence sense; the record does not support that label. Yet he was plainly a multiply situated source. He was a former participant in the online field, a guilty cooperator awaiting sentence, an ongoing FBI helper, a witness preparing with prosecutors, an anonymous public persona, and a private person whose undisclosed civil identity remained protected. His testimony cannot be reduced to any one role. The epistemic task is to understand how the roles interact.

The KUBARK source may conceal the service that still governs him. The cooperating witness openly discloses the institution with which he now cooperates, but the depth of that relation remains partly inaccessible: the transcript repeatedly avoids details of his other FBI work, and a sidebar addresses the sensitivity of what he may say. The structure is therefore simultaneously disclosed and sealed. The jury knows there is an ongoing relation; it does not receive its full contents. The visible testimony is surrounded by an institutional remainder.

That remainder is not incidental. It is part of the witness’s aura of access. He appears as someone who came from inside the earlier digital network and now also moves within a law-enforcement structure. He is a bridge between two otherwise inaccessible systems. His authority comes partly from double placement. The witness is valuable precisely because he can translate one field into the categories of another.

【きょうの旧約聖句: Day 220】

十日後のことであった。
主（しゅ）の言葉がエレミヤに臨（のぞ）んだ。

エレミヤはカレアの子ヨハナンと、彼とともにいる軍のすべての隊長と、身分の低い者から高い者まで民（たみ）のすべてを呼び、彼らに言った、

「あなたたちがあなたたちの願いをそのみ前に示すためにわたしをそのもとへと遣（つか）わした、イスラエルの神、主はこう仰（おお）せになる、

『お前たちがこの地に留（とど）まるなら、わたしはお前たちを建て、引き倒すことはせず、お前たちを植え、引き抜くことはしない。
　わたしはお前たちに下（くだ）した災（わざわ）いについて思い直したからだ。

　お前たちは恐（おそ）れ続け、今も恐れている、バビロンの王を恐れてはならない—主（しゅ）の言葉。
　わたしがお前たちを救（すく）い、彼の手からお前たちを救い出すために、お前たちとともにいるからだ。
　わたしがお前たちに憐（あわ）れみを示すので、バビロンの王もお前たちを憐れみ、お前たちを自分たちの地に帰らせる。

　しかし、もしお前たちが〈わたしたちはこの地に留（とど）まらない〉と言い張って、お前たちの神、主（しゅ）の声に聞き従（したが）わず、〈いや、わたしたちは戦（いくさ）に遭（あ）うことなく、角笛（つのぶえ）の音（ね）を聞くこともなく、パンに飢（う）えることもないエジプトの地に行って、そこに住もう〉と言うのなら、さあ、今、ユダの残りの者よ、主（しゅ）の言葉を聞け。

　イスラエルの神、万軍（ばんぐん）の主（しゅ）はこう仰（おお）せになる。

　もし、お前たちがエジプトへ行こうと固（かた）く決意し、そこに行って住みつくなら、お前たちが恐れている剣（つるぎ）がエジプトの地でお前たちに追いつき、お前たちが心配している飢えが、エジプトでもお前たちについて来て、お前たちはそこで死ぬ。

　エジプトに行ってそこに住みつこうと決意している者はみな、必ず、剣によって、飢えによって、また疫病（えきびょう）によって死ぬ。
　彼らのうち一人として、わたしが彼らに下す災いから逃れる者も生き残る者もいない』」。

エレミヤ書 42:7-17
（聖書 原文校訂による口語訳　フランシスコ会聖書研究所訳注）

[Today’s Old Testament Verses: Day 220]

Ten days passed before the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah.

Then he called Johanan, son of Kareah, his army leaders, and all the people, from the least to the greatest, and said to them:

Thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, to whom you sent me to offer your petition:

If indeed you will remain in this land, I will build you up, and not tear you down;
I will plant you, not uproot you; for I repent of the evil I have done you.

Do not fear the king of Babylon, as you do now.
Do not fear him—oracle of the LORD—for I am with you to save you, to rescue you from his power.
I will take pity on you, so that he will have pity on you and let you return to your land.

But if you keep saying, "We will not stay in this land," thus disobeying the voice of the LORD, your God, and saying, "No, we will go to the land of Egypt, where we will not see war, nor hear the trumpet alarm, nor hunger for bread. There we will live!” then listen to the word of the LORD, remnant of Judah:

Thus says the LORD of hosts, the God of Israel:

If you are set on going to Egypt and settling down there once you arrive, the sword you fear shall overtake you in the land of Egypt;
the hunger you dread shall pursue you to Egypt and there You shall die.

All those determined to go to Egypt to live shall die by the sword, famine, and disease:
not one shall survive or escape the evil that I am bringing upon them.

The Book of Jeremiah 42:7-17
(New American Bible Revised Edition)

📰"COUNTRY LIFE, England – Feb. 2, 1989
CR: T. GoodGOING ROUND IN CIRCLES
by RALPH NOYESScientists remain baffled by the mysterious circles appearing in cornfields in southern England. First noted in 1980, the phenomenon, in which circular areas of corn are flattened, is increasing, not only in the number of circles appearing but in the complexity of patterns they form.THEY began again in May 1988, the circular patterns of disturbance which have been turning up in crop fields, mainly in southern England, since at least 1980. To some local farmers —Lt-Cdr. Henry Bruce, for example, who farms near Winchester—they now seem as regular as the cuckoo, as predictable (and exasperating) as untimely frost. To others who are not so regularly haunted, these mysterious circles have come as a great surprise. On a farm near Yatesbury in Wiltshire four were discovered in a field of barley, shortly before combining last year.All farmers, of course, are familiar with the damage done to standing crops by wind, rain, summer whirlwinds and thoughtless visitors. The pliable crops to which we give the generic name of corn are particularly vulnerable; and it cannot be coincidence that the disturbances with which this article deals have occurred mainly in cornfields and mostly between May and September, when bad weather does most damage to such crops. But weather and mankind tend to leave ragged patches of no particular shape, not precisely defined areas of flattened crops, swirled into nearly perfect circles and looking as if a giant biscuit-cutter has been used to make them. Still less do we expect complex patterns of circles.But this is what has been happening since 1980. In that year, single circles, each about 60ft in diameter, were found in three fields of grain near Westbury. They were reported in the Wiltshire Times, and two were carefully surveyed. Writing in his internationally respected Journal of Meteorology, Dr G. T. Meaden of Bradford-on-Avon concluded that we might be witnessing the effects of a kind of summer whirlwind; but nothing like it seems to have come to scientific attention before. In 1981 a row of three circles was found in a field near Winchester, the central one about 60ft in diameter, the other two about 25ft each. Suspicion was briefly directed at Army helicopters, but careful enquiries ruled that out.Since then the phenomenon has blossomed. Not only are more of these disturbances (beautiful to behold though expensive for the unfortunate farmer), appearing each year but the patterns into which they fall are also becoming more elaborate. As well as single circles of several sizes, there are doublets and triplets of circles, some of the triplets being laid out in a triangle. There have been a number of quintuplets—a large central circle surrounded by four smaller ones, regularly placed. There have been quadruplets, and one or two irregular “swarms”. Most surprising of all have been the ringed circles—simple circles contained within a ring or even two rings of disturbance. In all these complex arrangements there are interesting combinations of the “swirl” of the grain—for example, a central circle swirled clockwise but surrounded by a ring in which the grain lies anti-clockwise. More than 400 circles have been reported since 1980, and more than a dozen different patterns have been recorded. 1988 being perhaps the most remarkable year so far.The highlight was the discovery on July 15 of a quintuplet of circles in a field just across the A4 from the foot of Silbury Hill, near Avebury, Wiltshire. This was followed by the appearance of a second quintuplet about 10 days later, followed a week after that by three simple circles, bringing the total to 13 in this unusually troubled field (which lies in the full gaze of one of the busiest roads in Wiltshire). During the same summer, and also near Avebury, a swarm of 13 circles turned up in the area of Yatesbury; and quintuplets were found on Allington Down and near Beckhampton, both in Wiltshire.Elsewhere, that haunted field of Lt-Cdr. Bruce’s near Winchester suffered first a triplet of circles and then a striking “double-ringer”, the traces of which could still be clearly seen after combining. There were occurrences farther afield, too, not only in Hampshire, Somerset and Wiltshire but also in Leicestershire (one) and Suffolk (one), and two or three of them have exhibited patterns that have not been seen before.The most determined drive towards a solution to the puzzle has been made by Dr Meaden, whose series of articles in the Journal of Meteorology from 1981 to date are classics of meticulous observation. We owe it to Dr Meaden, who has examined more than 300 of the 400 or so circles so far reported, that not only helicopters but also hoaxers must be ruled out in the great majority of cases, and he is searching for an explanation in meteorological terms. His careful scientific reasoning can be followed in the Journal of Meteorology, obtainable from him at 54 Frome Road, Bradford-on-Avon, Wiltshire BA15 1LD (£1.60 per month, inclusive of postage).Other, wilder, guesses abound. The western counties of England, where these things have mainly been observed so far, are engagingly haunted territory, rich in henges and stone circles, steeped in romantic legends, criss-crossed by supposed “ley lines”, haunted by ufologists (if not UFOs), redolent of some of the best folk-tales outside the Celtic borders. It would have been astounding if we had not had some theories of a far stranger kind than atmospheric physics can offer. (A bibliography is available, free, from me, c/o COUNTRY LIFE.)At the other end of the spectrum, down-to-earth respondents to the many articles which have appeared in the national and local press have offered a range of earth-bound hypotheses: mating hedgehogs; vixens making nests for their young; the summer rituals of the rural British; the effects of a virulent fungus (possessing geometrical tendencies on a large scale); and military experiments.The only certainty at present is that the phenomenon exists and will doubtless continue to surprise us. Any opinions, photographs and factual reports (obtained without further disturbing the unfortunate farmers who suffer these things) will be gratefully received and passed on immediately to experts. Particularly welcome would be well-authenticated reports from earlier than 1980 and from areas outside the West Country.Circular Evidence by Colin Andrews and Pat Delgado is to be published in June by Bloomsbury Press.Photographs: 1, 2, the author; 3, G. T. Meaden. Photo captions:(Top) 1—The large central circle in a quintuplet of circles in a much-troubled field next to the A4 near Silbury Hill, Wiltshire.
(Above) 2—View of the whole field  3—The central circle and its two outliers in the same field."

text:
A strong, cohesive, and professional army does more than defend borders. It underpins the conditions necessary for long-term economic power:
- Security and stability — Investors, both domestic and foreign, require a minimum level of physical security and predictable order. Without it, capital flees or never arrives.
- Sovereignty over resources — In resource-rich regions like the Great Lakes, the ability to control territory and prevent illicit extraction or smuggling determines whether mineral wealth becomes national economic power or fuels a war economy that benefits others.
- Deterrence and bargaining power — A credible military raises the cost of external interference and strengthens a country’s position in regional negotiations, trade corridors, and strategic partnerships.
- Institutional credibility — An army that is respected internally helps maintain the broader state capacity needed for taxation, infrastructure, and policy continuity.

History offers many examples: states that lost effective military capacity often lost control of their economic future as well. Conversely, countries that maintained or rebuilt military strength frequently used it as a foundation for later economic development and strategic autonomy.

In the specific Great Lakes context, the logic is particularly sharp. A weakened national army reduces a country’s ability to protect its interests in a highly competitive environment driven by critical minerals, proxy dynamics, and external powers. Strengthening the army is therefore not only a security issue — it is also a prerequisite for future economic agency and sovereignty.

text:
July 14  Blessed Gaspar de Bono OM (Gaspar de Bono i Montsó, Gaspar de Bono i Manzón) Priest, Friar of the Order of Minims, Vicar Provincial of the Order. He was noted for his particular devotion to the Passion of Christ.
1530– 1604
.
Gaspar was born on 5 January 1530 in Valencia, the second of the four children of Juan de Bonom who had emigrated from Gascony and his wife, Isabel Juana Manzón (or Monzon), originally from Villa de Cervera in the Province of Lleida. Upon his birth, he was baptised at the nearby Church of St Nicolás. Having been born on the eve of the Feast of the Epiphany, he was named for one of the Biblical Magi.
.
Gaspar’s parents were very pious and very poor. His father was a linen weaver by trade but when his mother was blinded three years after his birth and became unable to help in the family trade, the father was forced to sell their home and his tools and took work as a grinder and reseller.
.
Every morning the couple attended Mass and offered their day to God. While the husband worked, the wife meditated or weaved. From this couple four sons were born and the parents resolved to give a better educational formation to one of them, Gaspar, for they noted the exceptional gifts in the child.
.
As a child, he developed a noticeable stammer, a problem from which he suffered his whole life. At the age of ten,Gaspar began working with a silk merchant but soon realised that his vocation was religious and began to study Latin while continuing to work to help support his family. In about 1545, he was admitted as a candidate to the Dominican Order but, just as he was about to enter their novitiate, he was talked out of this by a brother-in-law, after which he returned home.
.
At age twenty, Gaspar joined the army of the Emperor Charles V, in search of fortune. He served as a soldier for about ten years but continued to try and live a devout and religious life, by praying, saying the rosary daily, donating to charity and frequenting places of worship. As a military man he never swore or took the name of God in vain, something quite common at the time among his fellow soldiers. He was extremely vigilant even when he received visits from the most honorable of ladies. He avoided undignified companions. After the fulfillment of his duties, he would go to churches, hospitals and other places of devotion.
.
A strong devoté of the Most Holy Virgin, he prayed her Litany and the Rosary every day. He had also special devotion to St. Anne, St. Joseph, St. Vincent Ferrer and the Souls of Purgatory.
.
Once he was with a small company fighting in Lombardy and was attacked by the main body of the enemy's cavalry. Realizing he could not face the large group alone, he slowly retreated, all the while trying to kill some of the adversaries to do what he could to weaken the opposition. He did not notice a deep moat and fell into it, with his horse atop him. Already wounded by the fall, he received three blows of a halberd by an enemy soldier.
.
Left for dead, he turned to the Holy Virgin, promising to enter the Order of the Minim Friars founded by St. Francis of Paula if he were saved. And he survived miraculously. He returned to Valencia and was received shortly into Minim Monastery of St Sebastián at age 30 in the year 1560 and was ordained a priest in 1562.
.
Fr Gaspar soon became known for his virtue and strict compliance with the Rule of Life of the Order. He was available to all the people of the neighbourhood which he knew thoroughly. He was present to comfort his parents in their final hours, his Mother dying on 29 April 1583 and his father, a year later. He was soon named Master of novices for the Catalan Province of the Order, being responsible for the founding of a Minim Monastery in Barcelona. He was then elected to serve as Vicar Provincial. In 1602, at the insistence of the Archbishop of Valencia, Juan de Ribera (now honoured as a Saint) and against Gaspar’s wishes, he was elected Corrector Provincial (Regional Superior) of Valencia. He is said to have remained humble and austere; retaining his devotions and customs and continued to be noted for his prudence and charity throughout his life.
.
He died on 14 July 1604, the body being exposed in the conventual Church of St Sebastián de Valencia, miracles and wonders attributed to his intercession took place immediately. He was buried three days later under the steps of the main Altar. In 1835, after the suppression of the Monastery under the Napoleonic rule of Spain, the urn containing his bones was moved to the Church of St Nicolás, where he had been Baptized as a baby and enshrined under the Altar of the Chapel of St Raphael. Gaspar’s remains were damaged in 1823 and desecrated in 1936, so that only some bones are today venerated in the Parish of St Nicolás de Valencia.
.
Given his exemplary observance, his deep prayer, his patience, his humility and, in general, the set of virtues that characterised his life and the miracles attributed to his intercession, the Diocesan Information Process began very early. The cause suffered various vicissitudes and delays but finally on 10 September 1786, Blessed Gaspar was Beatified by Pope Pius VI . In March 1786 he was declared, by the Palma de Mallorca City Council, the most illustrious son of the City.
.
Eternal Father, I wish to honor Blessed Gaspar de Bono, and I give Thee thanks for all the graces Thou hast bestowed upon him. I ask Thee to please increase grace in my soul through the merits of this saint, and I commit the end of my life to him by this special prayer, so that by virtue of Thy goodness and promise, St.  Blessed Gaspar de Bono might be my advocate and provide whatever is needed at that hour. Amen.

text:
Greg Isenberg's "ambient businesses" and Bindu Reddy's 50-to-500-agent predictions are all over my feed right now.

The pitch: agents run the business, you check in every few days, work becomes optional.

I want this to be true.
I don't think it is, not for the people actually reading those threads.

Here's the part that gets skipped:

Someone still has to decide what those agents build, sell, and say in your voice. Fifty agents running one bad offer just produces fifty times the noise, faster. That's not leverage.

That's the content treadmill wearing a nicer outfit.

I run my entire business on 3 tools: Claude Code, Kit, and Typefully,

Not fifty agents. 3

Real leverage was never zero human decisions. It was fewer decisions, made well, running on repeat.

My newsletter pipeline touches AI at almost every stage, research, drafting, repurposing into threads and notes, and I still make the same three calls every single time: what's the idea, is it true, does it sound like me.

An army of agents can't make those calls for a one-person business, because those calls are the business.

"Ambient" is a good word for a business nobody's paying attention to anymore.

I'd rather run 3 tools I understand completely than 500 agents I have to babysit into relevance.

If your business ran on autopilot tomorrow, would you trust what it shipped without reading it first?

text:
Nobody touched him.
​
Second quarter, second career start, and he tucked the ball and ran. He planted. The knee went. Torn ACL, right leg, no contact involved.
​
His team won 42-0, their first shutout of a conference opponent in twenty years. He watched most of it from the sideline.
​
He was born in Austin, one of four kids. His father grew up in Salt Lake City and earned Eagle Scout, and that sash hung in the house all through his childhood. He earned his own.
​
The summer before seventh grade he started running drops and throws in the yard with his older brother, another quarterback.
​
Four varsity seasons outside Austin: more than 8,700 passing yards, 121 total touchdowns. As a senior he led the entire state of Texas in passing.
​
Auburn offered. Oregon offered. Penn State, Texas A&M, Tennessee.
​
He committed to Texas Tech in December of his junior year, to the staff that had offered him first.
​
He'd decided long before. He watched the Red Raiders beat Texas in overtime from the stands with his mom, went back to the hotel, and prayed about it.
​
Week 1 of last season, he broke a 64-yard touchdown run and hit 20.2 miles per hour. Eighth-fastest player in the country that week.
​
In September the starter went down at Utah. He came off the bench for 230 yards and two touchdowns in the second half. Final: 34-10.
​
Between thirty and thirty-five of his relatives were in that stadium. His dad's family never left Utah.
​
Then two starts of his own. Then the knee.
​
"If it's gonna be somebody that's going to be totally dedicated to getting back and attack the situation," his coach said, "there's nobody that attacks anything like Will."
​
The team moved on without him. Conference title. Playoff. Orange Bowl.
​
In the offseason they signed the top quarterback in the portal to start ahead of him. By spring that plan had fallen apart.
​
He couldn't do anything about any of it. So he did the only thing in front of him.
​
He wasn't cleared for spring ball. He threw anyway. Player-run seven-on-seven all summer with receivers who'd never caught a pass from him.
​
This month his coach told ESPN that if they were playing right now, he could do everything.
​
Full medical clearance: August 21. Week 1: September 5.
​
Nine months from a knee that gave out on its own, to QB1.
​
Will Hammond.
​
Now you see the whole picture.

text:
🙋🏴󠁵󠁳󠁯󠁫󠁿  CYNDI MUNSON vs. MIKE MAZZEI: OKLAHOMA NOW HAS A REAL CHOICE 🏴󠁵󠁳󠁯󠁫󠁿🙋

.............. The Republican primary is over. Gentner Drummond lost. Mike Mazzei is the Republican nominee for Governor.

Now Oklahoma voters face a remarkably clear policy contrast between Democrat Cyndi Munson and Republican Mike Mazzei.

Forget personalities for a moment. Look at the policies. All statements come directly from their public comments.

1. ABORTION

MUNSON: She says she will seek to repeal Oklahoma’s abortion ban by sending the issue to a vote of the people.

MAZZEI: He says life begins at conception, opposes abortion in all circumstances, and believes government has a duty to protect unborn life.

That is not a minor disagreement. It is a fundamentally different understanding of government's responsibility toward unborn human life.

2. EDUCATION

MUNSON: She wants substantially more funding for public schools, and AN END to Oklahoma’s private-school Parental Choice Tax Credit program, which she calls a “voucher scheme.” Parents, do you understand what this means? 

MAZZEI: He emphasizes reading proficiency, curriculum standards, accountability, and parental educational options. He supports greater educational choice rather than concentrating public policy exclusively on the traditional public-school system.

Again, two different philosophies: government-centered public education versus greater parental choice and accountability.

3. TAXES & GOVERNMENT SPENDING

MUNSON: She has opposed broad state income-tax reductions, arguing that they threaten revenue needed for public social programs, healthcare and other government services. 

MAZZEI: He proposes aggressively reducing Oklahoma’s income tax – initially from 4.5% to 3% – cleaning exemptions out of the tax code and ultimately asking voters whether Oklahoma should eliminate the state income tax altogether. He also advocates performance-based budgeting, spending restraint and eliminating government programs that cannot demonstrate results.

4. GOVERNANCE PHILOSOPHY

MUNSON: She desires more state programs, opposes any tax cuts, and says increased taxes are needed for her stated goal of more public (government) services.

MAZZEI: He desires to reduce taxation and require government to do more with less.

Elections ought to be about policies, not personalities, not campaign commercials, not whether you like or dislike the public persona of a candidate. 

Policies. Principles. Governance.

Republicans who supported Gentner Drummond for Oklahoma governor now face a different decision because the Republican primary ended on August 25. 

The November election is no longer Drummond versus Mazzei.

It is Cyndi Munson versus Mike Mazzei.

And on abortion, education, taxation and the size and role of government, Oklahoma voters are being offered two substantially different governing philosophies.

Read their positions. Examine their records. Then vote according to your principles and your understanding of the Constitution.

You may be hurt because your Republican choice for Governor, Gentner Drummond, lost to Mike Mazzei. 

But don't let your hurt make you abandon your conservative values and principles.

Oklahoma governors don't merely occupy an office. They determine the direction of our state. A vote for Cyndi Munson is a vote to turn our state more toward the socialist and increasingly communist platform of the Democratic Party. 

The choice for Oklahoma's next Governor is now abundantly clear. 

Wade Burleson

text:
Sylvan Goldman, an Oklahoma grocer, invented the shopping cart in 1937. He noticed that many of his customers, who were mostly women at the time, stopped shopping once their hand baskets became full.

Goldman realized that if customers had larger baskets, they could buy more items. But a larger basket would be too heavy to carry. So he placed a basket on wheels and used a folding chair as the frame.

At first, customers did not like the idea. Some women said the carts reminded them of baby strollers. Some men thought pushing a cart was not masculine.

Goldman believed the carts could work, so he hired men and women to push them around his stores. He also had employees offer carts to customers at the entrance.

Customers eventually started using them. Goldman patented the invention and made a large amount of money from it.

He later licensed the patent to another company, which improved the design and developed the telescoping shopping baskets commonly used today.

Photo: Goldman with one of his shopping carts in 1960.
